top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: HUGE MDI-Style Pulls AoE Leveling Veno Tank
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
This is a guide for MDI style leveling ( Giga pulling and doing high dmg (usually top in the dung unless playing with a primalist/cultist/templar) 

This class in this context is focused around applying debuffs and kiting. Plays very similar to VDH S1 in SL.

[talents]
Class tree priorities:
1. Lifeblood
2. Versatile and Deadly
3. Fury of Shadra & Avatar of shadra

Spec Tree priorities:
1. Regrow Exoskeleton.
2. Venomtip Poison
3. Impale.
4. Slimy stingers
5. Venomics

U can play Shadra's gift for 5% st if u want.  
Wicked Poison / Beetle poison is around 4 and 2% aoe respectively  , 2%/1%st.  
Drop Beetle poison for  Catalyst or Alacrity if you want.
U can drop points from the 2 points nodes to get beetle poison/ deadly sting if u want. 
U will be kiting most of the time even in higher keys it seems so how much u need defensive stats is still questionable.
U really want to be able live the grouping part of the pull after that you should be fine with decent play.

NOTE: EXPECT TO DIE A LOT WHILE LEARNING THIS. ESPECIALLY IF U WANT TO PULL LIKE A MADMAN (Which u definately can)

UPDATED TALENTS AFTER TESTING.

Alternative: Drop Venomancy Expert, Fury of anub and Mamba mentality for Blightcap Injestion.

[rotation]
USE: Spider Pheromones, Slow Poison + Blight Poison, and Venom Shield.
For The biggest pulls ( u can do most dungs in 2-3 pulls) 
1. Get impale as soon as possible
2. Run Slow + Blight poison (if u are going to be face tanking run Weakening Venom , for pure st Adrenal Venom)
3. Pull big, impale all the mobs to let ur healer catch up with the pull dmg. U can use Defenisves as needed 
what u do is:  1. Stun the mobs apply all ur dmg and slows. 2. Use defensive after stun ends. 3. after u see bad debuffs getting stacked on u or u feel like ur losing hp. Chitin rush away and kite.  Then go back in use stuns on cd, and defensives as needed depening on situation.
Perfectly u can tank packs for only 2-3 globals at a time especially with Venomics later u can basiacally play like SL S1 VDH.   And u will be top dps as well in most leveling scenarios.

AOE DPS Priority:
1. Expulsion
2. Cerapace Crash 1x for slimy stingers
3. Locust Swarm once the pack is grouped.
4. Barbed stinger on prio target (recast at 15 Stacks)
5. Keep Venomtip poison up  (usually you pull with this to soften the dmg you take when pulling)
6. Spam Cerapace Crash
7. Claw strike if no rage (shouldnt happen too often)

ST DPS Priority:
1. Barbed Stinger on CD(recast at 15stacks)
2. Deadly Stinger Hivebreak Proc
3. 5stack+ Expulsion
4. Keep Venomtip up
5. Spam hivebreak
6. Clawstrike if no rage.

[stats]
No idea yet.  For leveling prioritise stamina, agi, and armor. 
Agi is ur best overall stat as it provides armor, dodge, AP and SP, and crit. 
Best dps stat is hit rating till cap while leveling, spell power after that. 
Your base spell values are high enough to top dps every aoe pull.

[gear]
Will make gear list soon.


I recommend using 2 weapons - faster AS - more dot applications, and u can have 2x enchants at endgame. 

As encants use (Ninja's Focus + Strider or (whatever the spellpower one is))

[enchants]
SOON

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Optimal Build for Raids/M0
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
From testing and discussion amongst other MK players this seems to be the best build available for us for current available content. This is a build purely for level 60 and NOT levelling as Mountain Hammer is near useless in PvE and it is recommended to skip it entirely until 60 whereupon you respec into it to gain Earthen Avatar and Primal Guardian.

[talents]
The only talents I would consider optional and not integral to the build are Boulder Dash and Dreamslip from the Primalist tree, and Bash and Resources of the Earth from the MK tree. However, Replenishment is an extremely valuable asset to bring to a raid and not many classes can take it as easily as we can. If you were to take the point out of Replenishment (if someone in your raid was already providing it) then the best place to put it would be Tilling the Earth for the extra Expertise.

Another option would be to swap out Grove Guardian and/or Protector of the Grove for Earthmother's Blessing if you are worried about getting one shot however if something would kill you on top of the 30% extra health Earthmother's Blessing gives you when it activates - you still die. It is not a cheat death.

Alternatively, if you hate fun, you can swap out Boulder Dash and Environmentalist for Heavy Handed which gives you extra armour on your self heals. This does add yet another buff to keep track of and extra button to press when you're already GCD capped but can make the difference on high damage fights.

[rotation]
Your standard rotation is as follows:

1. Maintain Earth's Rage
2. Reapply Earthquake and Rock Barrier after they end (never before)
3. Keep Quake on cool down and Raging Earth applied
4. Geode Barrage with Aftershock if Earthquake is up
5. Seismic Smash to maintain Thane's Rage and fish for Quake/Aftershock procs
6. Wildclaw as filler

This rotation is pretty much the same for ST and AoE although most AoE situations will involve a lot more EQ opportunities to hold aggro on casters that won't stack or pull more groups.
Seismic abilities **other than Smash** should only be used to pull as they use far too much mana otherwise.
With a fast OH and proper play you should be able to maintain near 100% uptime on Rock Barrier in ST but make sure it falls off before reapplying to refresh Primal Guardian.

Our opener on bosses can be quite complex and some things are not very intuitive so here's an explanation for everything up until your second/third GCD of any given boss encounter. This is made a lot easier to time properly and pull off if you are the one pulling (with a timer).

1. Use Therazane's Rage at least 10s before the fight starts so you begin at max rage. The Primal Fury talent is great here to keep your rage up whilst not in combat
2. Use Rock Barrier 10 seconds before pull. This will make your Primal Guardian trigger at the start of the fight
3. Use Seismic Smash 5-8 seconds before pull to activate Thane's Rage and generate an Aftershock
4. Just Judgement of The Three Hammers just before pull
5. The following abilities, other than the last one, do not use the Global Cooldown (GCD) so should be cast at the same time but in this order: Mountain Avatar > Charge > Earthquake > Quake
6. If you are in Boon of the Bear (which I would recommend on any fight that you know you won't die to) use Primal Convergence, otherwise save it as a defensive ability
7. Proceed with rotation as normal

[stats]
Stat weights are a bit of a meme right now but it's currently understood that Strength/Parry>Stamina>everything else. Nothing deals enough damage to warrant going too tanky and everything you care about scales off of Str/Parry.

[gear]
There has been a lot of discussion on whether we want fast or slow weapons for this spec and I lean heavily into the camp of slow main hand and fast off hand. The argument for having double slow weapons relies on casting Wildclaw often since it scales off of the damage of both weapons. However, Terrasmash, Fury of the Earthmother, and Mountain Avatar make proccing Geodes EXTREMELY beneficial for everything that our spec wants to do. Therefore we want our OH to be as fast as possible to get as many of these off as we can.

The 3 set of Courage you can buy with Marks of Triumph is very nice to have, as well as any Imperial Plate (of Parry) crafted items you can get your hands on otherwise focus on your main stats of Str/Parry.

Here is my current/most recent gear setup for reference:
https://coa.ascensionlogs.gg/armory/James/Rexxar

[enchants]
These are self explanatory; take anything that gives you more of the stats you already want. Double Crusader on weapons.

[macros]
#showtooltip
/startattack
/cast [@cursor] Earthquake
/stopcasting
/cast Therazane's Rage

This is an example of what you want from a macro for this spec.
It is generally a good idea to bind /startattack into all of your main damaging abilities to make sure that you don't lose your target or stop attacking for any reason.
Using the [@cursor] prefix for Earthquake specifically allows you to instantly drop it wherever your mouse is without having to click to confirm the spell. Alternatively, if you're lazy, you can use [@player] to place it on top of yourself.
Adding /stopcasting to your Earthquake and Geode Barrage macros is recommended to avoid accidentally hard casting them whilst tanking as you cannot dodge or parry and whilst casting a spell so will be quickly deleted by whatever mobs are on you.
Also, since Therazane's Rage wants to be cast on cooldown in all situations I would suggest adding it to the macros for your most commonly used spells so it's done automatically and without the need for an extra button press/plate to spin.

#showtooltip
/cancelaura Boulder Dash
/cast Boulder Dash

Missclicking the funny boulder button can get you killed very fast since you cannot mitigate damage during the effect. This macro allows you to instantly cancel it with a second press.

[tips]
Earthquake has some quirks that make it so that you never want to cast it while it's already active as it deals damage through a debuff that is not refreshed by the new instance of the spell on the ground. For this reason you should always wait for your current Earthquake to dissipate before recasting.
Alternatively, in AoE situations, I find liberal usage of Earthquake to pull new packs or keep aggro on stray caster mobs to be extremely beneficial.

While you'll probably spend ~90% of your time tanking in Boon of the Turtle don't forget that other Boons do exist and have their own uses. The dodge chance of Boon of the Wolf (especially under the effects of Primal Convergence) can be stronger than the damage reduction afforded by Turtle in some situations. In other cases where you don't need to be as tanky; Boon of the Bear offers a high damage/threat option. Also, if you've done any amount of dungeon spamming I'm sure you'll have been victim to the amount of fear effects some of them throw at you, in which case Boon of the Lion is surprisingly useful for short bursts of utility.

Another, very niche, quirk that I've found is that Dreamslip seems to be one of the only things that work to drop combat on Captain Kromcrush if you're attempting a Tribute run without the costume.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: KOX Hellfire balanced AOE+ST M+ build
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
Great balanced build both for AOE and ST in dungeons and M+

[talents]
Hellstorm is not taken in this build due to it being slightly worse than your usual AOE Demonfire spender Flames of Xoroth and on top of that, there is a great talent to have instead of it which is [Punisher](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:704988) that helps with ST damage, especially while usuing your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300). One of the most powerful AOE in this build is Into the Maw that is used with both [Indiscriminate](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:704958) and [Shadowflame Forge](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:704989) 1/2 in this build which is enough to use [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) 3 times after applying your Hellmaw on your target. This way your Hellmaw spreads on 10 targets total right before exploding with huge damage

[rotation]
Always use your [Pestilence of Apocalypse](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:804786), don't forget to buff Str Mark and call your [Call: Hellfire Imp](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:804883). The Annihilation proc always takes priority to generate Demonfire stacks.
AOE with [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300):
Start with using your [Burning Rage](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:520295) before the pull. Firstly use your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) and right after that [Unleash Pestilence](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:801002) (try to always refresh it's duration by spending 4+ Demonfire stacks on Flames of Xoroth or Hellmaw) Then use one [Meatsaw](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:501508) to get 6 stacks of Demonfire and right after that apply your Hellmaw on the tankiest target and use enough [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) on your Hellfire target to spread Hellfire on every target that was pulled. If your [Unleash Pestilence](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:801002) is at 1-2 seconds until expiring then use your Flames of Xoroth to refresh it's duration and then continue spreading Hellmaw if needed. After spreading your Hellmaw on every target use Flames of Xoroth and then continue spamming [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) to stack Demonfire if your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) is still active and spend your Demonfire stacks on Flames of Xoroth if your Hellfire is still up.
AOE when you don't have your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300):
Use your [Meatsaw](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:501508) to gain Demonfire stacks and use them on Hellmaw spreading it 3 times by using your [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) 3 times on CD. In between of using [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) continue using your [Meatsaw](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:501508) to gain Demonfire stacks and Flames of Xoroth to spend your Demonfire stacks if your Hellmaw is still up, othewise use Hellmaw and spread it once again since it still blows up if the target dies dealing more damage than Flames of Xoroth.
ST with [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300):
Start with using your [Burning Rage](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:520295) before the pull. Firstly use your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) and right after that [Unleash Pestilence](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:801002) (try to always refresh it's duration by spending 4+ Demonfire stacks on Melt, Hellmaw and Skullsplitter) Then spam your [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) with 6 stacks of Demonfire until your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) ends. After your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300) ends, firstly spend your Demonfire stacks on Melt, then use [Demon Heart](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805669) and apply Hellmaw. Use your Infernal Strike to get Demonfire stacks and cast your [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) at 6 Demonfire stacks when it's not on cooldown before spending your stacks on Skulltaker since [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) deals great damage at 6 Demofire stacks thanks to Brimstone Flames. Try to keep Melt on the target all the time and reapply Hellmaw after the explosion.
ST when you don't have your [Hellfire Form](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:503300):
Use your Infernal Strike to gain Demonfire stacks and use them on Melt, Hellfire and Skulltaker. Cast your [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) at 6 Demonfire stacks when it's not on cooldown before spending your stacks on Skulltaker since [Seeking Flame](coa-skill:knight-of-xoroth:805671) deals great damage at 6 Demofire stacks thanks to Brimstone Flames. Try to keep Melt on the target all the time and reapply Hellmaw after the explosion.

[stats]
I am still not 100% sure about the prio, but imo it's something like this:
Strenght > AP > SP > Int > Stamina (try to get every single item with Strenght, but items with AP and no main stat are also great)
Items with Agility and Spirit are absolutely irrelevant.
As for the secondary stats you should consider getting enough Hit to play comfortably (at least get enough spell hit for now which is not that hard to get with Mythic gear):
Hit > Crit > ARP = Haste
Not sure if ARP or Haste is better for Hellfire, Either way it's better to get Hit or Crit

[gear]
Get yourself 6 pieces of Lightforge set, 2H weapon with either Strenght or AP and other items should be with Strenght. 
As for trinkets there are some really good ones like:
Ramstein's Lightning Bolts
Drakefury Scale
Hand of Justice
Cannonball Runner
Fighter's Seal of Eldre'Thalas
There are also some decent options that, in my opinion, fall slightly short of the trinkets mentioned above:
Draconic Infused Emblem
Briarwood Reed
Grace of the Herald
Witching Hourglass
Rose of Remembrance
Smolderweb'd Eye

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Cultist Healer M+ Ready
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
Heretic Cultist let you heal your whole party by doing MASSIVE DAMAGE so if you always wanted to be a dps but you are stuck in the healing prison, this spec is made for you.
If you want a video guide instead, I made one → https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=-rMi2co9cUE

[talents]
Lot of thing to say here. I'll start from bottom to top because the bottom rows are very important.

- First, we take **@Dark Prophet** because it is the most broken aoe healing ability. It does around 25% to 40% of your overall healing in dungeon.

- Next we have a choice between [Hand of Yogg-Saron](coa-skill:cultist:704476) or **@Void Barrier**. It really depends on your group composition. If you think you are going to need an extra defensive spell for your tank, take [Hand of Yogg-Saron](coa-skill:cultist:704476), otherwise, you can take **@Void Barrier** for the extra 100% buff on your [Void Shield](coa-skill:cultist:500715) .

- 3rd row, we are getting buffs to our healing ability and also getting **@Dark Chants** which makes **Black Blood** stacks an additionnal time during his duration and a reduce cast time of your aoe shield **Forbidden Ritual**.

- [Dark Veil](coa-skill:cultist:520345) gives us an emergency button for when you are out of everything and you are unable to heal someone. It does around 8k shield on someone for 5 sec which gives enough time to recover cooldowns. **@Saronite Cube** is good for **@Void Shield** usage.

- Finally, we don't have much to talk about, the rest of the talent are buffs to healing spells, we get **@As The Prophecy Foretold** for mana sustain, [Eldritch Eye](coa-skill:cultist:802049) which makes the next 4 instance (Thanks to **@Saronite Blessing**) of either [Malevolence](coa-skill:cultist:500714) or [Eldritch Mending](coa-skill:cultist:500711) instant cast. 
We do get **@Abyssal Covenant** which is a key talent for our healing. It allows us to convert our damage into heal to the guy your applied the buff on *usualy the tank* and also activate our biggest healing ability -> **@Dark Prophet**. Lastly, you will get a free instant **Eldritch Mending** every 3rd melee ability you cast, that can helps you heal your party without spending a CD on them.

[rotation]
- **Presence choice** : You can either play with **Presence of N'Zoth** , **Presence of C'Thun** or **Presence of Y'Shaarj**. 

- **Presence of N'Zoth** to get the extra Tentacles healing thanks to **Twisted Sanity** but it won't be much. It does around 2% to 4% of your overall healing but atleast you get big Tentacles on your back.
- **Presence of C'Thun** to get a nice and comfy 20% haste buff. 
- **Presence of Y'Shaarj** to get that extra overall damage on big pulls.

- For the buffs, you can run **Whispers of N'Zoth** of the 12% total stats. If you play with a Sun Cleric, you can use **Whispers of C'Thun** for the SP since they apply the 12% total stats themself.

Now for the fight rotation, it's pretty simple. You keep **Black Blood** buff on your party all the time and just press your damage ability. Prioritizing [Blade of the Empire](coa-skill:cultist:500720) since it's your main damage/healing ability, spend your sanity on [Entropic Slam](coa-skill:cultist:555351) in 3+ monsters fight or [Hammer of Twilight](coa-skill:cultist:805116) in singletarget/boss fight.

- [Malevolence](coa-skill:cultist:500714): This is an important spell because it applies to 5 people **Black Blood** which is your number 1 spell on your list to keep track on. Note that the Hot duration doesn't refresh if you repress the spell. So you usually press it twice to stack the hot and repress it when the hot is gonna fade ~1 sec before so you don't lose time.

- [Herald of the Depths](coa-skill:cultist:805120): Our only damage/healing burst spell. It increase your damage by 15%, which is nice, but the main part is it buff by 100% our absorption duration and healing over time effects. You get double value on your **Black Blood** duration.

- During heavy fight where your party is going to receive a lot of damage, you can pre-stack your sanity to 80 with **Satiate** or by keeping your sanity high with the previous fight so you can press early your [Herald of the Depths](coa-skill:cultist:805120).
There's multiple way to heal during this kind of fight. You either spam damage or since we are in Herald form, you can apply massive shield to your whole party with [Forbidden Ritual](coa-skill:cultist:800105) + [Void Shield](coa-skill:cultist:500715). This way gives your party around 3k to 5k shield which make the fight a lot easier in just 5 sec of applying shields.

- Tentacles ? Yes Tentacles. I usually play around [Tentacle of C'Thun](coa-skill:cultist:801153) for the damage and extra healing with [Twisted Sanity](coa-skill:cultist:706187) but [Tentacle of Yogg-Saron](coa-skill:cultist:802042) is nice to press in heavy damage fight where you have your **Herald** up and 2 stack of **Black Blood**, the 6% increased healing feels nice.

- [Gaze of C'Thun](coa-skill:cultist:500110): I use this spell on CD kinda except when I know there's big damage incomming and I want a healing burst in that window thanks to **Void-Touched** passive talent which is massive healing.

- Finally, for your mana and sanity usage, early in the game, where you are either not 60 and currently leveling or even when you are 60 and don't have that much gear/crit chance, you are going to use **Sanity Tap** a lot. Usually after every 3 to 4 gcd. It gives your 20% of your missing mana. Try to fit some Tap during your gameplay to not end up oom mid pull and let your party die. It requieres 20 sanity to press it ->[Blade of the Empire](coa-skill:cultist:500720) gives your 20 Sanity and [Malevolence](coa-skill:cultist:500714) 10.

[stats]
- After some testing, Crit > Str/AP > SP/Int > Haste feels the best and fun. You don't really need that much mana if you have enough crit rate for your auto to regen mana with the talent **As The Prophecy Foretold**

- With the stats choice, we can easily wear plates gear, which makes us tankier than running cloth/leather gear to get Int/SP.

- You want to get a big 2H weapon, as slow as possible and either lot of **Attack Power** on it or **Critical Strike + Strenght** to get max value of our class.

[tips]
If you have any question, you can ask them in chat on my twitch channel **https://www.twitch.tv/azvt_** or on discord directly, we have some channel made for that !

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: PvE Valkyrie for Dungeons (M+ with Video Guide)
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
This guide was created to help players who have picked up this specialization and want to perform well in PvE content. I am constantly adapting and updating it by studying other guides and analyzing what truly works best. These adjustments are being made for a few reasons: first, everything is still very new and we are constantly discovering new things; second, others often suggest options that ultimately seem superior and are worth considering here.

References used: https://coabuildhub.com/build/7e9d9222-bd9b-46f8-b6fa-2012abfb8654 (by DarkGuardian) / https://coabuildhub.com/build/687811f2-5314-47a6-b19c-153d3019a071 (by Daniel Ritter) / https://coabuildhub.com/build/7de24f09-dd6b-44e6-b143-b17bd860c422 (by Naerrix Couture) / https://youtu.be/IpDr4hiSI44?si=-Qz-sKzmFfj4Y4JP (by Hello Heroes Guild)
I'm listing those once you can check their own content too, they have their own profile and it's pretty good too, mine is focus on M+ design and for sure won't be always right, try by yourself what you think it's better for you.

The profile and link's that you found here are free to use and you can republish them too for your own domain, just cite ^^.

This build is engineered primarily for Mythic+ (M+) performance. While it functions well during leveling and some raid scenario, players must mind dungeon crowd-control (CC) profiles (such as STUNlet Monastery).

Adjustments are required for pure Single-Target (ST) content, though the fundamental playstyle remains mostly intact without significant damage loss.

Video Resumed Guide mentioned: (https://youtu.be/7TixqGYGt7A)

[talents]
Depending on the encounter type, choose between Divine Retribution and Knight of Dawn:

Divine Retribution: Simulates significantly higher in AoE/Cleave scenarios.

Knight of Dawn: Performs exceptionally well if played correctly, though less consistent in large pulls.

[overview]
Hi, I'm NxS and I've been playing WoW for a decades especially in BG's / RBG's and Arenas.
Also played at top level on Arena Tournament back in the days.
Here's my PvP Guide for the Reaper Class based on my experience. Feel free to leave a review ;)

⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ Video of the build : https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=AZBb9IE3WRo
⭐⭐⭐ Video Gameplay commentary : https://youtu.be/mdpzCNOsgiw?si=2cL2uBACr4RrdP3_
⭐ 157k dmg in Arathi at lvl 59 : https://image.noelshack.com/fichiers/2026/32/2/1785843700-157k.png

[talents]
## Harvest Tree

**Why play [Ruin](coa-skill:reaper:805198) + [Shudder Scythe](coa-skill:reaper:805708) ? **

The goal of this build isn’t just to maximize theoretical damage against a stationary target, but to maximize actual pressure in PvP: immediate burst damage, resource generation, sustain, and setup reliability.
Ruin remains a central piece because it significantly boosts the value of our primary offensive tools, particularly during windows where we chain Doomrend and Slaughter. Since the Reaper aims to concentrate as much damage as possible within a short window, Ruin directly improves our ability to convert an opening into a kill.
We pair it with Shudder Scythe rather than Blood Frenzy because Shudder provides multiple layers of value simultaneously. The spell deals 5 hits for a total of 150% Weapon Damage, but more importantly, it generates 5 Soul Fragments. Since 3 fragments are needed to form a Reaped Soul, this averages out to about 1.67 Reaped Souls per use. This accelerated generation immediately fuels the Reaper’s engine: more Reaped Souls, more Soul Harvest procs, greater sustain, and a better ability to chain together offensive actions without delay.

This is particularly important in PvP, where a fight is often decided in a matter of seconds. Blood Frenzy has greater raw damage potential if the target remains available for its entire duration, but its value is spread out over time and drops sharply as soon as the opponent kites, applies CC, uses a defensive ability, or breaks contact. Shudder, on the other hand, concentrates nearly all of its value into a single GCD: damage, fragments, Souls, and sustain are obtained immediately. In a short, chaotic fight, this reliability is generally more valuable than higher theoretical DPS.

This approach becomes even more effective with Soul Harvest and Soul Furnace. Each Reaped Soul generated provides additional damage and healing via Soul Harvest, while Soul Furnace further enhances this sustain. Shudder thus becomes an offensive ability, a resource generator, and an indirect defensive tool all at once. It is this concentration of value that makes the Ruin + Shudder Scythe package so powerful.

**Why not play Blood Frenzy ?**

Blood Frenzy remains excellent and can outdamage Shudder in a sufficiently long trade with good uptime. However, it doesn’t accelerate the generation of Soul Fragments or Reaped Souls and doesn’t directly feed the Reaper’s sustain loop. It essentially provides an additional layer of damage, whereas Shudder improves the build’s overall functionality.

In practice, Blood Frenzy is better suited to a playstyle focused on long trades and constant uptime, while Shudder is more consistent with a Reaper PvP strategy based on short windows, high resource generation, and a rapid transition into Doomrend and Slaughter.

**Why is [Darkrend Scythe](coa-skill:reaper:805205) being set aside ?**

Darkrend Scythe is very strong when you can maintain multiple stacks of the bleed effect, particularly with rotations that regularly use Crow’s Harvest or chain together multiple Doomrend casts.

In this PvP version, that’s not the case. Doomrend is used more sporadically, during prepared windows, and Crow’s Harvest isn’t integrated into the rotation. As a result, we rarely exploit the full potential of Darkrend’s 5 stacks. A single application is still decent, but it doesn’t justify sacrificing a talent that immediately provides damage, resources, and sustain.

Darkrend is therefore more of a sustained pressure talent, whereas this build aims to maximize a short kill window.

**Why is Redshade left out ?**

Redshade can be useful in builds focused more on sustained damage, Shadow damage, or prolonged pressure, but it adds less value to our main loop.

Our priority is to strengthen what allows us to quickly convert an opening into a kill: Ruin → resource generation → Doomrend → Slaughter, with Soul Harvest providing support. Redshade doesn’t contribute as much to this loop as Shudder and the related talents.


### **In summary :**

Ruin + Shudder Scythe is chosen because it offers the best balance between immediate burst damage, Reaped Souls generation, sustain, reliability, and synergy with Doomrend/Slaughter.

Blood Frenzy mainly offers higher theoretical damage over a long uptime.
Darkrend requires too much time and too many applications to reach its full potential.
Redshade provides less value to the build’s core loop.

For a general-purpose, aggressive PvP approach, Ruin + Shudder Scythe is therefore the most well-rounded package.


## Class Tree

**[Masochistic Rage](coa-skill:reaper:803030)+ Soul Harvest **
Offense: ★★★★★
Sustain: ★★★★
SS/Souls Synergy: ★★★★★
Utility: ★★
BG Opinion: Best All-Rounder
Why: Excellent balance between pressure, soul generation, and self-heal. You can engage, finish off a target, and then continue playing without being completely dependent on a healer.

**Soul Harvest + [Soul Furnace](coa-skill:reaper:805184)**
Offense: ★★★
Sustain: ★★★★★
SS/Souls Synergy: ★★★★★
Utility: ★★
BG Opinion: Best sustain / anti-focus
Why: Excellent in prolonged teamfights or when you’re frequently focused. Shudder Scythe constantly feeds Soul Harvest, and Soul Furnace maximizes this regeneration loop. Very strong for staying active for long periods between skirmishes.

**[Masochistic Rage](coa-skill:reaper:803030) + Painbringer **
Offense: ★★★★★
Sustain: ★★
SS/Souls Synergy: ★★★
Utility: ★★
BG Opinion: Full DPS / snowball
Why: Very good if your team lets you stay aggressive and you want to rack up kills. However, you sacrifice a large portion of your sustain, so it’s less effective if you often play far from healers.

**[Sinister Litany](coa-skill:reaper:805185) + [Ghost](coa-skill:reaper:705426)**
Offense: ★★★★
Sustain: ★★
SS/Souls Synergy: ★★★
Utility: ★★★★★
BG Opinion: Best utility / roaming
Why: Very useful for choosing your engagements, bypassing a fight, reaching the backline, or securing an objective. In BG, mobility and the ability to decide when to engage are worth much more than in a simple duel.

**Soul Harvest + [Sinister Litany](coa-skill:reaper:805185)**
Offense: ★★★★
Sustain: ★★★★
SS/Souls Synergy: ★★★★★
Utility: ★★★
BG Opinion: Excellent offensive hybrid
Why: You retain the full value of Shudder → Fragments → Souls → Soul Harvest, while adding better opening potential. Very good if you want to stay versatile without taking Masochistic Rage.

**[Sinister Litany](coa-skill:reaper:805185)+ [Masochistic Rage](coa-skill:reaper:803030)**
Offense: ★★★★★
Sustain: ★
SS/Souls Synergy: ★★
Utility: ★★
BG Opinion: Glass cannon
Why: Huge potential to quickly take down an isolated target, but poor endurance against an entire BG. Once your burst damage is spent, you have far fewer ways to sustain a long teamfight or take down multiple opponents in succession.

**1. Masochistic Rage + Soul Harvest — Best All-Around Choice**
The most balanced option for racking up kills without completely sacrificing sustain.

**2. Soul Harvest + Soul Furnace — Best for Team Fights / Anti-Focus**
Probably the most comfortable option for playing long games without a dedicated healer.

**3. Soul Harvest + Sinister Litany — Best Roaming/Offense Hybrid**
A great alternative if you prefer flexibility and openings over MR.

**4. Sinister Litany + Ghost — Best for Objectives / Roaming / Backline**
Less raw damage output, but excellent utility specific to Battlegrounds.

**5. Masochistic Rage + Painbringer — full DPS**
Very strong if your group protects you and you can play in “kill-hunter” mode.

**6. Sinister Litany + Masochistic Rage — glass cannon**
The most explosive build, but also the one that’s least forgiving of bad engagements.

[rotation]
**Souls management = Harvest King**

1) Open with Reap or Murder and harvest up to 3 Soul Fragments. 
2) Wraithblade if up and if you don't have any souls ready (use it on CD).
3) Doomrend to apply its anti-heal shield.
4) Reap as your basic filler between cooldowns. It feeds Soul Fragment generation.
5) Murder on cooldown while closing, or on a second target, for free extra Soul Fragments and to apply Ruin (Shudder Scythe upgrades it into a bigger fragment-generating hit). 
6) Keep Souls for the Slaughter rolling so your autos add Shadow damage. 
7) Slaughter the moment a target drops below 35% HP for the execute plus a Reaped Soul. 
8) Harvesting Grounds on a fleeing target, or a pack you want slowed. 
9) Sever to interrupt a dangerous cast. 
10) Harvest Time is your burst window when you can commit to a heavy trade.
11) Use Soul Strike if you need to survive combine with your defensives CD's such as Jailer's Bargain for example.

[stats]
Hit (melee/special, until your specials stop missing a +3-level target) > Expertise (until your attacks stop being dodged/parried) > Strength > Armor Penetration > Critical Strike > Haste

Just go for arena Gear and use good PvE trinket if you have some

Focus objectives & win ! 
It took my days to understand that objectives and winning gives way more exp.
The more BG's faster you are to win BG's, the more faster you'll level up and leveling on BG's only is quite fun on CoA

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
## Ever wanted to feel like a raid boss?

That's exactly what this build is about.

You're trading flashy burst damage for ridiculous survivability, allowing you to tank almost anything the game throws at you while still putting out enough DPS to stay relevant.

The build shines in every PvE scenario and can easily be adapted for PvP by replacing a couple of optional picks with Mana Burn.

Everything else is essentially mandatory. Every talent has a purpose and contributes to making the build as durable and consistent as possible.

If dying isn't part of your game plan, you've found the right build.

[talents]
This build focuses on consistency rather than burst damage. 
Every talent has been selected with one of four objectives:
- Increase survivability.
- Improve Felfury generation.
- Maximize Inner Demon uptime.
- Maintain strong threat while dealing competitive damage.

Many offensive talents were intentionally skipped in favor of defensive consistency. A dead tank deals no damage.
The Tyrant tree naturally provides excellent damage, allowing us to invest more heavily into mitigation without sacrificing clear speed.

**If you prefer a simpler rotation with one less button to manage, you can replace Tyrant's Gaze with Betrayer. While you'll lose some execute damage, Betrayer remains a solid alternative and is perfectly viable for players who value a smoother playstyle.**

[rotation]
### Multi-Target Rotation

**Hateforged Barrier** → **Burning Hatred or Blood of Mannoroth** → **Inner Demon** → **Felrend** → **Felrend** → **Sunder**  → **Sargeron Smite**

Use **Carve** whenever possible. Thanks to **Annuhilan Rituals**, a fully channeled **Carve** effectively costs only **1 Felfury**, making it extremely efficient. Follow it with **Fireball** to benefit from the empowered cast. The **Carve → Fireball** combo deals excellent AoE damage and should be used whenever you have the opportunity.

 ⚠️⚠️ **Warning:** The **Carve → Fireball** combo is a DPS gain, but it also comes with a survivability trade-off.⚠️⚠️

Because you're spending less Felfury with the combo**Felrend** and **Sargeron Smite**, you reduce your **Hateforged Barrier** uptime, gain fewer **Abyssal Conditioning** stacks, and spend more time channeling. If you're playing without a dedicated healer, I generally recommend sticking to the **Felrend + Sunder + Sargeron** rotation for much better consistency and survivability. See the discussion in the comments for a more detailed explanation.

Once an enemy drops below **35% Health**, prioritize **Tyrant's Gaze** to execute the target and quickly move on to the next enemy.

### Single-Target Rotation

The single-target rotation follows the exact same priority, with only two changes:

* Replace **Felrend** with **Twin Slice**.
* Replace **Sunder** with **Sargeron Smite**.

**Rotation:**

**Hateforged Barrier** → **Burning Hatred** → **Inner Demon** → **Twin Slice** → **Twin Slice** → **Sargeron Smite**

⚠️ **Never cast Sargeron Smite without Inner Demon active.**
 Doing so results in a massive DPS loss and significantly reduces the effectiveness of the build. Always make sure **Inner Demon** is active before using **Sargeron Smite**.

## 💥 Cooldowns

### Hateforged Barrier
Your most important defensive cooldown.
Keep it active as often as possible. Thanks to cooldown reduction, maintaining nearly permanent uptime is entirely achievable.

### Inner Demon
This build revolves around **Inner Demon**.
Never let it expire unless absolutely unavoidable.
Every aspect of your rotation is designed around maximizing its uptime.

### Burning Hatred
Primarily used to instantly generate Felfury and quickly reactivate **Inner Demon**.
Avoid using it immediately on every pull.

Instead, save it for:
* Long encounters.
* Large pulls.
* Recovering after losing Felfury.

### Blur
Reserved for boss mechanics or emergency situations.
Since **Blur** reduces your threat generation, always follow it with **Betray** to immediately recover aggro.

### Fel Bargain
Emergency button.
Only use it if your healer cannot keep you alive.
Without a Tinker in your group, this cooldown becomes significantly more dangerous.

[stats]
**Priority**

1. Hit Rating (until cap)
2. Agility
3. Stamina
4. Critical Strike
5. Haste

Agility is by far the strongest primary stat for this build, increasing both your offensive and defensive capabilities.

Because several abilities scale from weapon damage, using **two slow two-handed weapons** provides the highest overall performance.

Leather gear with Agility remains the best option.

[leveling]
Leveling as a Tyrant is extremely smooth and beginner-friendly. The spec has excellent survivability, allowing you to comfortably solo most quests and elite enemies without much difficulty.

Your main priority while leveling is to spam Felrend as your primary damage and threat ability while keeping Hateforged Barrier active whenever possible.

Although the build is capable of handling large pulls, don't get too greedy early on. Your gear won't be optimized yet, and overpulling can quickly overwhelm both you and your healer in dungeons.

Play it safe during the early levels, focus on maintaining your defensive abilities, and gradually increase your pull size as your gear and survivability improve.

By the time you reach higher levels and unlock the full build, you'll be able to comfortably chain large packs and fully take advantage of Tyrant's incredible durability.

[pvp]
The PvP version keeps almost the entire build unchanged.

The only recommended adjustment is replacing a few PvE-oriented talents with **Mana Burn**.

This allows you to heavily pressure healers and casters while maintaining the incredible survivability that makes Tyrant so powerful.


>_>

Tyrant truly shines as an objective-focused flag carrier. Your incredible survivability makes you extremely difficult to kill, allowing you to secure and transport flags with confidence.

While this build is perfectly capable of winning most 1v1 encounters, don't get baited into unnecessary fights. Your real value comes from playing the objective.

Capture bases, carry flags, waste the enemy team's time, and force them to commit multiple players just to bring you down. Winning the battleground is far more satisfying than chasing kills.

[tips]
# ❌ Common Mistakes
* Letting **Inner Demon** expire.
* Casting **Sargeron Smite** without **Inner Demon**.
* Forgetting to refresh **Hateforged Barrier**.
* Wasting **Burning Hatred** at the beginning of every fight.
* Using **Fel Bargain** too early.
* Using **Blur** without immediately following it with **Betray**.
* Ignoring **Tyrant's Gaze** below 35% Health.
* Focusing too much on DPS instead of maintaining defensive uptime.

# 💡 Advanced Tips
* Always start difficult pulls with **Hateforged Barrier** already active.
* Plan your **Burning Hatred** usage instead of treating it like a regular cooldown.
* Prioritize maintaining **Inner Demon** over squeezing in one extra offensive ability.
* Use **Felrend** and **Sunder** aggressively on large pulls to stabilize threat before your DPS unloads.
* Save **Blur** for predictable boss mechanics rather than random damage.
* A good Tyrant anticipates incoming damage instead of reacting once health starts dropping.
* **Tyrant's Gaze** is more than an execute—it helps reduce incoming damage by removing dangerous enemies from the fight faster.
* Don't be afraid to chain large pulls. This build truly shines when fighting multiple enemies at once, where its survivability and threat generation outperform most other tanks.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
*Updated after recent rework. Gameplay got a lot clearer. Adjusted talents a bit. Updated rotation and leveling tab.*

## Overview
Time spec is **NOT** that easy. Like at all. You need to invest some **time** *(heh..)* to master the art of stance swapping. And since its a caster obey main rule.

**ABC - always be casting**

This spec is built around uptiming your HoTs on your group and dealing moderate AoE damage with the help of stance swapping every 5 seconds. 

Time brings several unique buffs and spells in it's kit to your m+ run:
**Fray Magic** - Interrupt
[Continuum Restoration](coa-skill:chronomancer:801271) - Mass dispell
[Hasten](coa-skill:chronomancer:801304) - Power Infusion for your dps (if [Unmaker of Realities](coa-skill:chronomancer:706107) is taken) or both for you and your dps (if you take Maker of Realities)
[Resynchronize](coa-skill:chronomancer:804495) - Mass res if your group wiped or you can res yourself while in combat to consume battle res charge.

## Raid buffs
48 spirit or 37 intellect.

## Survivability 
[Temporal Anomaly](coa-skill:chronomancer:806315) is an insane defensive to keep you alive.
[Clasp of Infinity](coa-skill:chronomancer:805847) and [Waves of Time](coa-skill:chronomancer:801277) should be more than enough to keep enemies far from you while your tank is gathering your pull.

## Damage output
Most of your damage output will be [Aeon of Oblivion](coa-skill:chronomancer:806293) + [Ripple](coa-skill:chronomancer:806296). This combo does moderate damage because of your passive level 50 capstone: [Eternity Warper](coa-skill:chronomancer:806301). 
In single target encounters in addition to dps ripple casts, uptime your Decomposition debuff. Can add spamming some [Epoch](coa-skill:chronomancer:801275) casts with [Aeon of Oblivion](coa-skill:chronomancer:806293) active.

[talents]
## F.A.Q
### Why no **Improved Reverse Wound** *(class row 2)*?
- There's no much point in it, because you are overwhelmed in your [Endless Sands](coa-skill:chronomancer:806338) procs, becasue of [Wonders of Time](coa-skill:chronomancer:560541) procs. It take you only 2 stacks of [Endless Sands](coa-skill:chronomancer:806338) ative for your [Reverse Wound](coa-skill:chronomancer:801303) to be in your GCD range. Mostly you always have instacast stored anyways.

### Why **Unearthed Pools** *(class row 2)*?
- Even if we are not casting [Unmake](coa-skill:chronomancer:804418) that much we still get plenty of mana discount for **most** of our spells, even [Ripple](coa-skill:chronomancer:806296).

### Why no [Temporal Focus](coa-skill:chronomancer:806165) *(class row 6)*
- It is highly situational button to press, mostly useless. Can take it in specific dungeons, unlearn **Timewalking** *(class row 8)* in exchange.

### [Hasten](coa-skill:chronomancer:801304): Maker or Unmaker *(class row 7)*
- You always Hasten your DPS. **ALWAYS**. You just decide do you need hasten aswel *(you get 20% haste back if you target your ally)* or you go full-damage external. Never [Hasten](coa-skill:chronomancer:801304) yourself, you will drain fast and there is no circumstance when you need it.

### [Infinite Shield](coa-skill:chronomancer:520457) vs [Gravity Bomb](coa-skill:chronomancer:501820)
- [Infinite Shield](coa-skill:chronomancer:520457) does insane ammount of your overall healing keeping tank alive at all times. Since tank is your 85% overall healing done to its impossible to drop this talent in exchange to [Gravity Bomb](coa-skill:chronomancer:501820) juicy mass grip mechanic. Higher key level higher damage your tank will take.
*Most of the time you will LoS big packs anyways so they will stick in one place anyways.*

### [Epic Recovery](coa-skill:chronomancer:706098)?
- Yes. This talent is your game-changer. Even if it casts only Rank 1 [Epoch](coa-skill:chronomancer:801275) it still applies buffs from our [Eternity Warper](coa-skill:chronomancer:806301). More info in **Rotation** segment.

### Why no [Endless Sands](coa-skill:chronomancer:806338)?
- This talent is redundant, because of [Wonders of Time](coa-skill:chronomancer:560541). It's proc rate is kinda high, because we are constantly uptiming our [Accelerated Recovery](coa-skill:chronomancer:800857) and [Aeon of Renewal](coa-skill:chronomancer:806290) HoTs.

### Why no capstones in spec tree?
- I tried to play with them. Honestly. But all these talents either redundant or useless in general, even though they are fun in tooltips. [Buy Time](coa-skill:chronomancer:801280) is a huge disappointment. The only potential take is **Converge the Infinite** but there are so little highly AoE encounters in m+ for it to be vailable. [The Vast Infinite](coa-skill:chronomancer:706083) is a good capstone, but its gated with useless talent. Could be taken if it was swapped places with [Buy Time](coa-skill:chronomancer:801280).

### Why no [Fabric of Time](coa-skill:chronomancer:806299)?
- You almost never want or need to swap faster than aeon's regular 5 second cd. Your **Through the Aeons** forces you to swap every 8 seconds only. Your [Epoch](coa-skill:chronomancer:801275) base healing is not as impacted as you think for you to be starved in aeon swapping. 

### Possible swap-overs:
- [Temporal Focus](coa-skill:chronomancer:806165) vs **Timewalking**
- **Displacement** vs **Ideal Time**
- [Continuum Restoration](coa-skill:chronomancer:801271) vs **Displacement**
*You can pretty much rotate **Displacement**, **Ideal Time**, [Continuum Restoration](coa-skill:chronomancer:801271)* between each other.

[rotation]
## Core
- Uptime your **Through the Aeons** buff via stance swapping.
- Uptime your [Infinite Shield](coa-skill:chronomancer:520457) and **Timeguard** on your tank.
- **Temporal Restoration** buff should be active for additional mana regen.

### Main 
- Keep [Accelerated Recovery](coa-skill:chronomancer:800857) active on your group at all times.
- Extend it with [Fortify Timeline](coa-skill:chronomancer:804491).
-  [Aeon of Renewal](coa-skill:chronomancer:806290) + [Epoch](coa-skill:chronomancer:801275) spam casts to stack Renewal HoT on your target and your group via [Epic Recovery](coa-skill:chronomancer:706098). Stacking mechanic is similar to Mage's Ignite DoT. I'm able to stack it to 2.5k per tick.
- [Aeon of Protection](coa-skill:chronomancer:806292) + [Epoch](coa-skill:chronomancer:801275) spam casts to stack damage absorb on your target and your group. *(capped at 20% of target's health)*
- [Aeon of Renewal](coa-skill:chronomancer:806290) + [Ripple](coa-skill:chronomancer:806296) for aoe healing.

All your rotation consists of last three steps. You just decide what's more effective for your situation: damage absorb or renewal HoT. You can remove your [Aeon of Resilience](coa-skill:chronomancer:806291) from your bars if you never plan to do raiding. This aeon is useless in dungeon content.
You should get WA for **Ideal Time** tracking. **IT** doesn't get consumed from [Accelerated Recovery](coa-skill:chronomancer:800857) and [Ripple](coa-skill:chronomancer:806296) casts *(and **Decomposition** dot)*. You can do some insane AoE dps with **IT** + [Aeon of Oblivion](coa-skill:chronomancer:806293) + [Ripple](coa-skill:chronomancer:806296) damage if you learn to track the procs. All your [Accelerated Recovery](coa-skill:chronomancer:800857) ticks will crit, same as all [Ripple](coa-skill:chronomancer:806296) ticks combined with [Aeon of Renewal](coa-skill:chronomancer:806290) or [Aeon of Oblivion](coa-skill:chronomancer:806293). *([Eternity Warper](coa-skill:chronomancer:806301))*


*Additional options:*
- [Reverse Wound](coa-skill:chronomancer:801303) with 5 stacks of [Endless Sands](coa-skill:chronomancer:806338) for emergency or high target healing.
-  If you are experiencing high-aoe ticking damage on your group you can apply renewal hot from your [Aeon of Renewal](coa-skill:chronomancer:806290)+[Epoch](coa-skill:chronomancer:801275) on your group targetly 1 by 1, because [Epic Recovery](coa-skill:chronomancer:706098) applies only rank 1 renewal, which is bad, but it still stacks.
- Cast [Infinite Clone](coa-skill:chronomancer:804492) before heavy healing and use [Rewind](coa-skill:chronomancer:801294) afterwards to restore some of the spent mana or health.

Most of the times it is way more than enough to keep your group alive but if you are in heavy-aoe encounter. You can add some [Correct the Mistake](coa-skill:chronomancer:572352) casts if necessary.

### Ripple + [Eternity Warper](coa-skill:chronomancer:806301)
- [Aeon of Renewal](coa-skill:chronomancer:806290) - Good choice if you encounter ticking damage or middle-heavy aoe damage.
- [Aeon of Protection](coa-skill:chronomancer:806292) - Should be exactly timed for specific mechanic. Highly situational.
- [Aeon of Oblivion](coa-skill:chronomancer:806293) - Your main source of damage and the most impactful cast of [Ripple](coa-skill:chronomancer:806296). You do some damage while channeling and heal afterwards for high ammount if your group suffered some damage while channeling.
- [Aeon of Resilience](coa-skill:chronomancer:806291) - please don't...

[overview]
Grovekeeper is an easy to play DPS/Healer hybrid that summons Treants whenever it melee critically strikes, which explode for AoE damage and healing. It reaches peak power at lvl 57 when you unlock the Treant talent, but it is still very good before that point. It can top DPS and healing meters just by pressing 2 or 3 buttons, and provides powerful buffs such as Bloodlust and 20% crit chance. Your party will love you for playing this class.

[talents]
Rock Barrier can be taken instead of Mineralization for solo play.

[rotation]
Spam Wildclaw to proc as many treants as possible, cast an instant cast Earthquake once every 9 seconds, use Seismic Crash if you need to generate rage and to upkeep the spell hit chance buff for your party. Cast Seismic Wave in AoE. That's pretty much it.  Cast Primal Awakening (Bloodlust) and Tree of War along with your stat buff totem when your party needs to burst down a powerful enemy.

[stats]
Crit Chance is really the only thing that matters, as treants are the bulk of your dps and healing and you want to spawn as many as possible. Crit > Strength > Haste is your stat priority. While leveling and as a fresh lvl 60, I would recommend using a 2-handed weapon as it helps generate bonus rage. Slower weapons hit harder with Wild Strike, but faster weapons let you spawn more Treants. Once you have extremely good gear and have solved your rage problems you can consider swapping to fast dual-wielded onehanders, as they will let you spawn many more Treants.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
PvP Gladiator build prioritizing utility, survivability, and burst damage. Cycling through strong, low CD offensive cooldowns for big burst damage as a win con to close out sustained fights.

[talents]
Clinch Brawler guarantees a Centurion Strike crit so try to play around that, using Net Shot and Chivalry for big burst damage on the opener. 

Calculated Strike allows your Spear Throw to do respectable damage along with the 50% MS effect which you'll usually look to take advanage of in the opener. Reprisal isn't really reliable against non-melee classes since polearm won't be proccing the ability itself very often. High weapon damage, slow swing speed weapons are preferred for Centurion Strike burst. Valiant Effort could  be replaced with something else if you don't find value in it. 

Always look to root and slow people inside Glorious Arena. Comboing the with Grand Entrance is more burst on top of your Net Shot + Chivalry + Centurion Strike crit rotation. Currently the Heroism talent is bugged, so I'm taking Close Combat atm. Standard being on GCD is still very nice to swap between them as needed. In pvp Valiance is used very often, but the stun resist banner is pretty great too in teamfights. In a 1v1 melee brawl you can't go wrong with the healing banner.

[rotation]
Ideal opener is Spear Throw -> Net Shot -> Standard of Valiance -> Chivalry -> Centurion Strike -> Glorious Arena -> Grand Entrance. Keep track of Glory stacks with Heroic Effort so you don't end up with Ram on a full CD while you're sitting on 3 Glory stacks. Try not to use Battle Rush in the opener if you don't have to, it's important to trade mobility with the opponent, so if you're using it in the opener when you don't have to you're a lot more liable to being kited. 

Don't forget Linebreaker. It basically works like Shattering Throw, breaking immunities and has a -25% armor reduction debuff with only a 1 minute cooldown. The armor debuff can be hard to play around, only lasting 5 seconds.

[stats]
Strength = Stamina ≥ Agi  Gladiator gets a lot of raw damage from strength, but agi is also a great stat that you can't go wrong with as it gives you a lot of benefits. Your main win con is playing around the Net Shot + Centurion Strike burst which has guaranteed crits built in. Having crit is still good though, your sustained damage becomes a real threat when Grand Entrance and Ram also start dealing big numbers.

[gear]
Conquest Point PvP gear can be bought at booty bay. Honor gear is bought at your main towns' (Orgimmar or Stormwind) PvP vendor. These pvp items have higher resilience and pvp power than bloodforged so make sure you get them. These vendors sell enchants too and PvP trinket as well.

[leveling]
Pull big with Tower Formation and a polearm, Centurion Strike and Broad Sweeps for big groups off adds. Raise Shield will be your primary way of getting Reprisal off since slow polearms can't proc it on it's own consistently enough.

[pvp]
You have a lot of defensives to cycle through. You're a lot better at fighting melee than ranged, so look to check those classes and use keep relevant banners up (slow, stun resist, or healing usually, sometimes disarm resist). Counter Stance is basically a full heal so long as you get parries off, you can use this against pets too for a free full heal. Turn the Blade against other melees, Brace against Barbarians in the opener is good to avoid their Stun + Crush combo.

Using a Standard of Spellwarding in the middle of a group of casters you can't go wrong with, either. It's a deceptively strong way for gladiator to find value in a teamfight.

Here are all the macros I use, It's built to avoid having to avoid using an input on stance switching.

[tips]
Trade mobility with players, use your gap closers in response to their own mobility or CC. Don't waste advance, shrug it off, or battle rush if you don't need to. Do not Net Shot the same player immediately off cooldown; 15 seconds isn't enough time for CC DR to fade away, and they will only be rooted for 1-2 seconds. Spear Throw should be used before big bursts, as most classes have some form of sustain and will probably respond with big defensive buttons in response to your damage.

Standard of Spellwarding is a great utility option in big teamfights. Throw it in the middle of the enemy backline for free value if they have a lot of casters.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Nanobots, Explosions and Zap!
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
**Help your group overcome challenges with your Nanobots, Beacons, Explosions and Zap!**
*Don't be a healbot*

Always rotate your Augment, use explosive on 2+ targets, piercing during single target fights and stim when your group requires more green numbers from you. Keep your Nanobot Reconstruction and Nanobot Swarm on tank, mana regenerating bots on self and refresh all each minute. Position yourself a few yards from the tank, so the whole group benefits from your beacons. Keep one Replenishment Beacon up at all times. If you know there will be group damage incoming, you can prepare the group with shielding beacon and overcharge it for a group wide shield.

**PET**
Remember to put your Sentry Turret when the fight starts (beware it auto shots your target, so don't do it too early if you have the boss/trash targetted). You can cast Sentry Turret while casting something else.
Use ZIGGI-6K (your signature pet) at all times. It does a lot of damage compared to other pets and passively heals with that damage. Even when you're running solo, it's not worth to use the bear, instead, throw your misdirect nanobots (Swarm) on your Sentry Turret and let it tank for you, once it's down just put a new one and repeat.
If your pet dies or decides to go on its own journey somewhere, you can resummon it instantly after using Basic Intuition.
Watch your pet's mana from time to time, if it's getting low, pop its recharge ability, preferably during downtime. If you find yourself forgetting about pet's mana recharge, macro it with Air Strike, it's less optimal, but you can forget about that chore.
Don't use your pet's Revitalizing Aura, the healing provided is not worth the mana used.

**DPS**
For aoe don't waste your mana on Scrap Shot, but use Sticky Bomb on cooldown and make sure you have your explosive augment on for aoe auto shots. Pop an airstrike when you know the fight will be long enough. Use battle turret for big pulls if you know the group can stay alive while you're in it or have someone else control it.
For single target use piercing augment, throw a Sticky Bomb on cooldown and spam Scrap Shots as long as mana is not an issue.
Remember that you don't auto shoot while moving, so try to find a comfortable place and stay there. If you need to reposition yourself, do a few steps and stop for a shot, distance depends on the attack speed of your weapon, you'll get to feel it.

**Healing**
As previously mentioned, keep your nanobots on the tank, they will heal the whole group when they are in range. Zapping someone with nanobots is a guaranteed crit that leads to more aoe healing. Always prioritize Zap! for direct healing, if the tank takes heavy constant damage throw them a Med Pack (remember it has a pretty short range, so you might want to position yourself close enough to the tank, but far enough from the enemies to shoot them). Use beacons and overcharge them whenever needed (more details in Rotation). If somehow the group requires more healing, or someone is spread too much and stays out of range of beacons or nanobots (you can pull them with pet's active ability - see macros), shoot em with Repair Shot. For healing heavy fights swap to Stim Augmentation over explosive/piercing one.

**Resources**
Keep mana nanobots on yourself at all times and position yourself in replenishment beacon. Overcharge in a single Replenishment Beacon might not give you much mana (based on your total, if recharge costs more than 10% of your mana, it's even gonna drain you), so try to overcharge 2 or more whenever you can.
You should be fine without Mana Module, so use Power Module on yourself - it increases your dps by a lot. *Don't be a healbot*

**Crowd Control**
Your main two sources of important CC are
- Macro Gravity Zone - 2 min cooldown aoe slow leading to a 6s stun. Very strong on big pulls, it's also always good to use it after calling an air strike, so the mobs don't leave the zone before it crashes.
- Noise Box - 1.5 min cooldown aoe interrupt, it's close range unfortunately, but if you see a group of casters far away and the group doesn't LoS them, use your Rocket Boots and interrupt them.

All other tools are very situational. 
Discombobulate! can be used to interupt an important cast, but it won't prevent from casting after the cc ends and even if you're the only person targetting that enemy, your turret will l likely shoot them and end the disorient, unless you macro a mouseover.
I strongly suggest not using Deploy Blast Mine in a stack of mobs, as it knocks back both them and your group, messing up what the tank has prepared. The only good use of it is to bring stray enemies back to the stack, but the preperation part makes it usually not worth it.

[talents]
If you notice that you rarely use an Air Strike, try using it, really. If you still don't and have that one player in your group (or yourself) going down all the time, put 2 last points of Tinker to the right side of the tree.

[rotation]
If the tank stops to gather a pack or engages a boss, pop an air strike, throw sticky bomb, put down your sentry turret and start placing beacons. Remember that all beacons except Shield can stack, both their passive and overcharge effect, so never stack two shielding ones.

- Shield Beacon - start with it, in an emergency situation your overcharge will apply a shield
- Replenishment Beacon - always aim to have at least one up (you can have more than 1, they will stack, both passively and after an overcharge)
- Restorative Beacon - only if the group takes constant damage higher than your nanobots output, or your Zap! is far from getting off cooldown and you know you will need more aoe healing. If that's not the case, it's better to hold 1 beacon stack off cooldown for Alarm Beacon, or if it's not needed - throw down another Replenishment Beacon.

If the pull looks scary, pop your Macro-Gravity Zone on tank, it will slow the mobs and lead to an aoe stun.
If there are lots of casters, or any of the mobs has an important cast (eg. Hex), cast your Noise Box.
If you notice someone gets Charm, Fear or Sleep, or you know enemies are going to throw those at you, pop an Alarm Beacon.

[stats]
Always prioritize intellect as it boosts your ranged attack power, healing power, crit strike rating and mana (the more mana you have the more you regenerate with beacons!)

Intellect > Spellpower > Crit Chance > Haste > MP5

[gear]
While leveling, don't force yourself into using mail armor only. If a cloth with more intellect drops, be happy about it!
Treat your melee weapon as a stat stick for int and try to pair it with a shield for more survivability.
The attack speed on your gun matters the most, as you proc your agumentations with each shot. My suggestion would be [Precisely Calibrated Boomstick](https://db.ascension.gg/?item=2100)

[leveling]
On low levels mana is your biggest problem. Overcharge might cost more than it returns with a single beacon. Until level 40 use Clockwork Pet for 20% mana back every minute, then Ziggi comes shining with your Graftbolts passive, but if you keep getting mana starved, feel free to keep Clockwork until you notice you don't need its extra mana.

[macros]
Pet controlling macro (I use it on scrap shot, so your pet won't do a first hit if macro'ed on Sticky Bomb):
#showtooltip
/use Scrap Shot
/petattack

Pet's instant heal + pull (I have it bound with Clique):
#show Minicopter-Z
/use [@mouseover, help, nodead] Minicopter-Z

There's my weakaura in the comments that shows:
- active Augmentation 
- Nanobot Recharger on you
- Zap! off cooldown 
- Module buff missing

[tips]
If you start to hate the sound of a gun (fast firing auto shots + sentry turret), put a crossbow transmog on it. Less tinker vibe, but more sanity preserved.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
This is an AoE-focused build with decent single-target for bosses with CDs. I've only been playing Primalist since the project started and have tried min-maxing different builds for each melee spec.

[talents]
Key talents here are Pulverize, Elemental Berserker, Totemic Echoes, Torn to Shreds, Spiritual Frenzy, Wild Carnage, and Totem Warrior.

Flex talents can be Wild At Heart; this talent is only good if you can keep your rage up to spam Wildclaws fast enough. If you need more single-target damage for raids, remove Wild Carnage with Rylak's Blessing.

[rotation]
Key Rotation:

Open with Grove Guardian>Totemic Smash> Primal Shred>Boulder Dash>Seismic Spike. Then spam Wildclaws until Totemic Smash is off CD.
 
Maintain Primal Shred and Torn to Shreds on all targets for rage/procs, and keep Wild Carnage buffed up every 6s by using Seismic Spike.

ST: Same opener, but instead of Seismic Spike, use Seismic Crash unless you need to cleave. Pop Primal Convergence and Savage Frenzy to increase DPS. 

*Grove Guardians is uncapped aoe dps and should always be taken.

[stats]
Attack Power and Strength will be your top stats. 

Crit will be your best secondary stat since we use Wildclaws as a substitute for attack speed.

Be sure to get hit capped and some expertise.*




* Still working on bis gear list and stats.

[tips]
I highly recommend running your pet on passive and macro /petattack into your key ST abilities.

BIS Pet: Wolf; it has a 20s AOE attack power buff on a 40s CD and an additional 20s 10% attack power buff on a 5-minute CD.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Competitive 1v1 Arena / BG Necromancer PvP Guide
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
Currently, the Animation tree offers the only truly viable spec to compete at a high level in PvP on Conquest of Azeroth. Because of the inherent risk of Necromancer becoming completely overpowered if over-tuned, the class has historically seen heavy tuning. However, with the right setup, Animation offers top-tier minion pressure, control, and explosive burst.

*Abomination and Winds of Northrend are currently dead talents in this build.*

**This build uses 6 Ghouls.**

Currently testing a promising BG version that is outperforming this version in BG.



**For more information on how to become the most imdominatable Necromancer, you can join IMMORTAL Necro-only Guild. 

Lvl 40+
https://discord.gg/rXeQ684Ft**

[talents]
Talent selection varies slightly based on your personal preference, the current meta, and whether you are queuing 1v1 duels or multi-target Battlegrounds.

**Death’s Due:** Less valuable in BGs, but theoretically useful in 1v1s to purge invulnerabilities. However, extensive testing shows it currently fails to reliably purge effects like the Venomancer’s invulnerability. It is recommended to drop this talent until further bug fixes land.

**Gravebound Champion CD Reduction:** Skip this for 1v1s, as rounds end far too fast to get a second cast. It holds much more value in drawn-out BGs.

**Overwhelming Force:** The superior option for baseline Mana and Runic Power generation.

**Phylactery:** Promising on paper, but currently untested in top-tier play and rarely utilized effectively. May be very strong in 2v2 and 3v3. 

**Frost Wyrm Pathing:** Frost Wyrm burst is simply too powerful to pass up. To reach it, you are forced to path through a dead talent: Winds of Northrend (Lichfrost Slow).

**Fetid Ward:** A solid defensive option, though further testing is required to confirm if it outperforms alternative defensive talents.

**Depravity vs. Mindless Fury:** Depravity is currently the stronger pick, though Mindless Fury can be considered if you are heavily stacking Haste.

**Tomb King vs. Bone Wrath:** Tomb King provides significantly higher impact during your primary burst combo.

**Unrelenting:** Turns your Crypt Swarm into a machine gun for Runic Power generation.

[rotation]
## Buffs & Pre-Fight Setup

Minions = 6 Ghouls.


### Baseline Buff Sequence

Keep these active at all times. Use a /castsequence macro to cycle through them quickly before 1v1 rounds or upon spawning in BGs:

Fetid Ward

Greater Grim Mandate

Greater Razorice

Greater Chill of the Tomb

### Combat Stance & Auras

**Assault Stance:** Keep this active continuously for the +5% Critical Strike Chance and increased movement speed for your Ghouls.

**Frozen Reliquary: **Save this for when your Mana pool is completely depleted to maximize the missing-mana scaling benefit.


### Core Opener & Rotation

Pre-Fight Prep: Drop your Summoning Ritual and channel Siphon Mana on your Ghouls to secure an early resources

**Summon Archers:** Always open by summoning your Skeleton Archers. They boost your Haste, deal damage from range, and build early Mana and Runic Power.

**Apply Harvest Plague:** Cast Harvest Plague immediately to begin siphoning health. The DoT tick actively prevents stealth classes from resetting the fight.

**Summon Heavy Minions:** Call forth your Tomb King and Plaguefather.

**Execute the Burst Combo:** Once your opponent commits to the fight and enters melee range of your army or you think you can kill them, pop your macro burst (Unholy Frenzy + Gravebound Champion + Frost Wyrm + Any racial trait) while commanding all ghouls to attack.

[stats]
## Gear & Stat Hierarchy

**Stamina:** Priority #1 for PvP survivability to prevent getting burst down in stun locks.

**Intellect: **Primary stat for raw Spell Power, minion scaling, and Mana pool size.

**Spell Hit Rating:** Mandatory up to the PvP cap (4% / ~32–36 rating at level 60) so crucial CC and burst spells do not miss.

Haste / Critical Strike: Secondary stats to stack based on personal preference (Crit for burst potential, Haste for faster cast cycles).

I've moved away from Crit and have focused on Haste, we can get down to 0.5 sec on a Ghoul summon. Ghouls also go berserk with the extra Haste. Feels much better than crit.

[gear]
Horde/Alliance Insignia for CC cleanse (you can buy this tricket with Honor at the PvP vendor). *This is Goated.*

Main thing is to stop the perma CC from some classes you will face in 1v1.

Always buy PvP gear with honor and start stacking PvP Power to stand a chance. 

Once you are level 60, you can spam BGs and the Call Board Daily for Honor and that will help you get the base PvP needed.

[macros]
Macro I use since it has 3 instant casts that don't trigger global CD and one instant cast that does at the end. 
 
(Unholy Frenzy + Gravebound Champion + Frost Wyrm + Any instant cast racial trait).

Copy and paste the macro below but you will need to remove or replace Arcane Torrent if you are not a Blood Elf:

#showtooltip Animate: Frost Wyrm
/cast Arcane Torrent
/cast Animate: Frost Wyrm
/cast Gravebound Champion
/cast Unholy Frenzy

[tips]
## Utility & Advanced Tactics

**Defensive Tithe Window:** Pop Bone Tithe at around 50% HP. This allows you to stack the shield while maximizing incoming heals from Fetid Ward and Command Attack from Ghouls.

**Gravebound Defensive Offense:** Weave Gravebound Champion into your burst phase to reduce incoming damage while adding another body to your minion army.

**Whenever your attack commands give you a free cast proc:**
Cast Blight if the target still has a large health pool.
Cast Frost Lich to snare fleeing enemies and/or generate a fast burst of Runic Power.

**Runic Power Dumping:** When your Runic Power caps out, spam your Command abilities.

**Minion Recovery:** If your army gets wiped, immediately cast Call of the Grave and resume spamming Ghouls.

### Disruption Control:

**Ghoulify:** Exceptional for catching targets in BGs and interrupting spell casts while your army attacks.

**Mass Grave:** Instant cast at 50+ Runic Power. Serves as a clutch, instant-cast AoE fear to turn the tide when swarmed.

**The "Entomb" Execute Combo:** Entomb an enemy at ~20% health, then instantly follow up with Death's Due. While niche, it provides a flashy execute option.

[overview]
Ranger Archery is first and foremost NOT a replacement of Hunter. So if you are looking for the hunter playstyle you wont find it here.

This usually gets me to 4-7k dps on ST and much more in AoE.. It does however, vary. Theres a lot of positioning to be aware of at all times.

[talents]
The most impactful talents is by *FAR* [Incendiary Shot](coa-skill:ranger:524870) It not only adds damage in AoE but also ST rotations so it stays no matter what. I have yet to try out 'Headshots only' for increased precision shot damage however.

[rotation]
Keep [Skirmish](coa-skill:ranger:802039) and [Serrated Shot](coa-skill:ranger:500073) Up at ALL Times.

Spend only on 5 Advantage points.

Cast [Incendiary Shot](coa-skill:ranger:524870) on CD
Cast [Precision Shot](coa-skill:ranger:500075)
Cast [Deadshot](coa-skill:ranger:520227) 
Cast [Skullpiercer](coa-skill:ranger:802036) ONLY if Skirmish is about to run out, or you cannot get in minimum range for a Precision Shot

ST: [Quick Shot](coa-skill:ranger:500074)

AoE: [Hunting Shot](coa-skill:ranger:801191)


Quiver: [Skirmisher's Quiver](coa-skill:ranger:801069)

[stats]
Prio:

Hit (cap)
Attack Power
Agility
Crit
Haste

[gear]
For pre-raid PvE Best in slot, I generated one on BiSBeard.com


**Dungeon Grind BiS Link**
https://coa.bisbeard.com/b/ZKoGwqKumjnXx2

**BiS with Reptutations and Crafted items included**
https://coa.bisbeard.com/b/JeYTzDI23JBGdH

[enchants]
Ninja Focus
+15 Agil on off hand
Crit / AP enchant on Ranged

[leveling]
Personally, I recommend Dungeon spam. Dont bother trying to level with this in the open world.

But if you are dead-set on leveling, Either you take Farstrider as it seems to do a lot better than this spec in low levels. Or you can always drop a point in [Resourceful] to lower the CD of Snapseed & Crippling shot to keep distance. You will not be able to zoom-tank major groups as easily but with some range management, not impossible. I also recommend Toxic / Searing Quiver for leveling. The same rule of thumb applies to rotation to keep Skirmish up and try to refresh it with full advantage spenders. Another great talent pick is Forest Dweller in higher levels to keep yourself in action longer.

[overview]
## **Witch Hunter - Houndmaster Guide**

## The build planner website is currently outdated. Some skills, talents, and their descriptions are missing or don't match the current version of the game

Houndmaster is a straightforward, pet-focused spec that excels at single-target damage. It's easy to pick up, has a smooth rotation, and performs very well in Heroic and Mythic dungeons, especially on bosses and other priority targets. Throughout Phase 0, it's been one of the specs I've enjoyed playing the most.

One of Houndmaster's biggest strengths is its excellent survivability. Between its Tonics, self-sustain, and durable pets, the spec is surprisingly resilient. It also brings a good amount of utility through Traps and Brands, giving it tools that can be useful in a variety of dungeon and raid encounters.

The recent change allowing Sixfold Shot to proc Shadowblast has been a huge improvement. It made the rotation feel much smoother and more engaging, giving the spec a much better overall flow than before.

That said, the specialization still has a few rough edges. [Quickdraw](coa-skill:witch-hunter:804193) currently feels underwhelming, dealing relatively low damage even with the 50% Critical Damage talent and Phase 0 gear. In addition, Lethal Pursuit is still bugged despite the recent fix—the stacks appear correctly, but they don't currently increase your Hounds' damage. Until it's properly fixed, I don't recommend taking the talent.

Overall, if you're looking for a spec with strong boss damage, solid survivability, and a simple but satisfying playstyle, Houndmaster is an excellent choice. While its AoE damage is only average, its consistent single-target performance more than makes up for it in most PvE content.
