[rotation]
I'm still experimenting with the optimal rotation, but so far I've found two different openers depending on how long the boss fight lasts.


### Long Fights (2+ minutes and the debuff is need it)

If the encounter is expected to last more than one minute, start by applying 5 stacks of Pommel Smash while dropping a Death Trap at the same time, since Death Trap does not trigger the Global Cooldown (do this only if the raid need it).

Unfortunately, the Pommel Smash buff only lasts 30 seconds (pls devs increase it to 60+), so keeping it active can be a little awkward since you'll need to briefly move into melee range before returning to your optimal positioning.


### Short Fights (no need for debuff)

If the boss will die quickly, simply skip the Pommel Smash setup and go straight into the normal priority rotation


### Priority System

The rotation is priority-based rather than a fixed sequence.

1. Unleash Hounds — Always your highest priority. Keep this active as much as possible for the Shadow Damage, Haste, and pet buffs.
2. Houndmaster's Call — Cast whenever it's available or whenever it procs from the 5% passive (remember to use Caltrops, for some reason proc a loot the pasive).
3. Shadowblast until reaching 5 stacks.
4. Cast Sixfold Shot, then immediately queue Quickdraw as Sixfold Shot finishes casting (see the macro section below).
5. Repeat the priority.

### Burst Cooldowns

For burst windows:

- Use Surging Tonic together with Slayer's Mark.
- Cast Decimate only after you've already used Unleash Hounds and Houndmaster's Call so your pets are fully buffed.

If the boss is Undead, use Holy Water Tonic together with Surging Tonic. The two effects stack, resulting in extremely high burst damage.


### Resource Management

Use Dark Regeneration whenever your Rage drops below roughly 50% or if you're starting to run low on mana (which generally shouldn't happen if you're mostly casting Shadowblast).

During very long fights and if your gear is low, you may eventually run out of Rage. When that happens, you'll need to rely on Tonics or weave in a few Darkslayer casts between Shadowblast casts to recover resources.


### Situational Abilities


**Brand of the Profane**

- Generates no threat, making it safe to keep on the boss whenever your raid benefits from the additional Hit Chance.

**Brand of the Damned**


- Intended for execute situations, but at the moment it simply not that good.
- Personally, I think it should activate at 20% health instead of 10% to make it more useful (pls devs).

**Scourge Trap**

- Deals excellent damage against Undead enemies.
- However, its long cooldown limits its overall impact.

**Caltrops**

- Recently nerfed, but still useful when tanks are kiting or repositioning adds.
- have no GCD
- Remains a strong PvP utility ability.



### AoE Rotation

I'm still testing different AoE rotations, so if you find something stronger, feel free to share it.

For now, this is what has produced the best results for me:

1. Make sure you have plenty of Lesser Hounds active to maximize cleave damage.
2. Cast Shadowblast once to activate your pets.
3. Place Shadow Trap and Caltrops.
4. Start casting Darkflock.
5. If Darkflock procs during the first slow cast, immediately cast it again to enter the fast-casting loop.

Your AoE damage improves significantly against 5 or more targets, since Feast of Talons becomes active.

That said, Houndmaster's AoE damage is currently nothing exceptional, and you should expect other specs to outperform you on large pulls.

## Macros

**Sixfold Shot + Quickdraw**

#showtooltip Quickdraw
/stopmacro [channeling:Sixfold Shot]
/cast !Sixfold Shot
/cast !Quickdraw


This lets you spam the same button whenever Sixfold Shot procs while automatically casting Quickdraw as soon as the channel finishes.

Note: If you spam the macro too aggressively right as Sixfold Shot starts, the channel can still occasionally get interrupted. Be careful not to mash it too early.


**Pommel Smash + Death Trap**

#showtooltip Pommel Smash
/cast Pommel Smash
/cast Death Trap

If you decide to use Pommel Smash in your opener, this macro will automatically drop Death Trap at the same time since it doesn't trigger the Global Cooldown.


**Vault + Caltrops**

#showtooltip Vault
/cast Vault
/cast [@cursor] Caltrops

If you prefer, you can replace @cursor with @player depending on your preference, Caltrops don't use a GCD so u can use it at coldown.



**Burst Macro**

#showtooltip Surging Tonic
/cast Surging Tonic
/cast Slayer's Mark
/use 14
/use 13

Uses your full burst setup with a single keypress. Slayer's Mark does not trigger the Global Cooldown

**Finally u can put /petattack wherever you want (I use it on shadowblast)**

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Flameweaving: The Phoenix Healer
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
🎵 🔥🔥 [Pyromania - Cascada](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=EsdXPPp8dNk) 🔥🔥 🎵

Flameweaving transforms our destructive fire magic into a force of restoration. While its core toolkit excels at sustained single-target healing, the specialization truly shines through its versatile and engaging resource management. As we heal and deal damage, we generate **Embers** - a secondary resource that fuels a variety of powerful and flexible abilities. Whether we need burst healing, team shielding, or extra damage, smart Ember management gives us the flexibility to adapt to every encounter.

You'll love the Flameweaving Pyromancer if you enjoy:

- **FIRE EVERYWHERE**
- Having a Phoenix pet
- Nearly infinite mana
- Secondary resource management
- Weaving damage into your healing rotation

[rotation]
**Mana**

You'll rarely need to worry about mana after level 30 thanks to a combination of different passives and buffs.

- **[Ashen Priest](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=707432)** maintains 20% of your mana regeneration while in combat while also granting **[Replenishment](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=1257670)** whenever you critically heal, restoring 5% mana to yourself and your party.

- **[Ashen Skin](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=504720)** increases your in-combat mana regeneration by an additional 60%.

- **[Shazzrah's Boon](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=807126)** restores 2% of your total mana whenever you spend an Ember, providing excellent passive sustain alongside **[Seal of Al'ar](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=808012)**, a buff we can apply to ourselves and others which restores mana every 5 seconds.

If you or a teammate ever begins running low on mana, **[Essence of Malygos](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=802120)** restores 36% of total mana over 9 seconds.

---

**Core Abilities & Gameplay**

Flameweaving isn't built around a rigid rotation. Instead, success comes from understanding your toolkit and maintaining enough Embers to flex into whatever the situation requires.

Nearly every healing or damage spell that **doesn't consume an Ember** generates Heat.

**100 Heat = 1 Ember**

Throughout this guide, abilities that consume an Ember are marked with 🔥.

---

**Mana Only**

**Phoenix Pet -** **[Phoenix Egg](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=800796)**

Your Phoenix should be active at all times. It lasts 60 seconds and pulses light AoE healing every 5 seconds (3 seconds with this build). Beyond its healing, several of your abilities require your Phoenix to be active.

*See the **Tips** section for the WeakAura I use to track its duration and prevent it from expiring during important moments.*

**Emergency Cooldown(2 Mins) -** **[Kael's Command](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=800816)**

Requires your Phoenix to be active. For 10 seconds, your Phoenix pulses powerful AoE healing, making this your strongest answer when multiple party members begin dropping quickly. Don't be afraid to use it proactively during heavy group-wide damage.

**Fast Heal -** **[Kindle](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=803825)**

A quick, medium-strength heal with no Ember cost.

**Slow Heal -** **[Cinderheart](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=502052)**

A slower but significantly larger heal with no Ember cost.

**Shield -** **[Inferno Barrier](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=535651)**

An instant single-target shield with a short cooldown. Best applied to the tank between pulls rather than during heavy combat.

**AoE Damage / Healing -** **[Cleansing Flames](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=681374)**

**Our bread and butter.** This spell does an incredible amount of heavy lifting by dealing moderate damage while simultaneously healing and shielding allies in a cone.

Don't let the small visual effect fool you - the cone is far more generous than it appears. Position yourself to hit enemies while simultaneously healing and shielding your tank and nearby allies.

**Large AoE Damage -** **[Meteor](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=500652)**

An instant-cast AoE with a cooldown. Drop this into large enemy packs before beginning your Cleansing Flames spam.

**Ember Generator -** **[Lava Shard](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=503239)**

An instant-cast ranged nuke with a 10 second cooldown that immediately generates **1 Ember**.

Use this on cooldown whenever you aren't Ember capped. If you're already sitting at maximum Embers, hold it until you've spent one to avoid wasting generation.

*See the **Tips** section for a basic WeakAura cooldown tracker if you'd like one.*
---

**🔥 Ember Spenders**

**High Priority**

**🔥 Instant Heal -** **[Ember Touch](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=520320)**

An instant medium-strength heal with no cooldown. Excellent for saving fragile party members when there's no time to cast Kindle, or whenever you have Embers to spare. Use this liberally.

**🔥 Group Shield -** **[Phoenix Dive](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=706854)**

An instant AoE shield with no cooldown.

Use this frequently between pulls or whenever you have excess Embers to cushion incoming damage before it happens. It shields allies in a medium-sized area around your target and requires your Phoenix to be active.

**Lower Priority**

**🔥 Single Target Damage -** **[Explode](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=502060)**

Decent nuke if you have excess embers and literally nothing else to do.

**🔥 Damage over Time -** **[Blaze](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=534604)**

Keep this on bosses if healing is under control and you have spare Embers.

**🔥 Line Damage / Healing -** **[Ignis Ultimatus](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=280570)**

My class talent capstone of choice. After a short cast, unleash a massive line of fire that deals heavy damage to enemies while simultaneously providing moderate healing to allies caught in its path.

While it's generally not worth spending an Ember on cooldown, it becomes an excellent choice whenever your positioning allows you to hit several enemies while also healing multiple allies. Think of it as a more powerful version of Cleansing Flames that looks badass.

**🔥 Multi-Target Damage -** **[Flames of Neltharion](https://db.ascension.gg/?spell=535512)**

Hits your target and two nearby enemies.

In practice, it's usually better to be casting Cleansing Flames or almost anything else, making it a very low-priority Ember spender.

---

**Typical Pull Strategy**

Before each pull:

- 🔥 Apply **Phoenix Dive** to shield the group before encounters.
- Refresh **Phoenix Egg** if necessary.
- Apply **Inferno Barrier** to the tank if you can spare the global cooldown.

Once combat begins:

- Open with **Meteor** against large packs.
- Position yourself so **Cleansing Flames** strikes enemies while covering the tank and as many party members as possible.
- In easier content, Cleansing Flames alone will often handle the majority of your healing.
- When heavy group damage is incoming, activate **Kael's Command** to stabilize the party.
- As incoming damage increases, spend Embers aggressively on **🔥 Ember Touch** and **🔥 Phoenix Dive** to stabilize the group.

[stats]
Spirit + Crit are your core priorities.  Anything else is gravy.

Critical heals give us many synergies like mana regeneration and free shields.

[tips]
**Phoenix Egg Duration Tracker**

Your Phoenix is the cornerstone of the Flameweaving toolkit. If it expires, you lose access to several important abilities and a significant amount of passive healing.

This WeakAura displays your Phoenix's remaining duration, making it much easier to maintain 100% uptime.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Warden PvP Skirmisher GOD Build
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
**Introduction**
If you are going Warden, you already know that you aren't here to run into 10v10 as a frontline tank, nor are you spamming aoe spells in range like many casters.
In fact, other classes will generally underestimate you because you deal almost no damage during the initial buildup phase and you are so squishy that you can get two-shotted by many other DPS classes when caught out of position.
But that is to your advantage when you learn to play right.
Wardens need to weave range and melee seamlessly as if playing hunter and warrior simulataneously in classic WoW.

Your primary roles and effectiveness are:
- Chasing down targets
- Fighting small skirmishes (1v1, 2v2, 3v3)
- Stalling as you run around and forcing people to chase you while you soften them up before going in melee range

As such, in big scale battles, just play a typical range building Scattered Stars and spamming Lunar Lance (LL).
Look for opportunities to go in for a quick kill then get out again.
If pulled in against a crowd, just immediately get out; don't even try to fight - run away while getting a few hits in.

In 1v1 or 2v2 you shine the brightest.
You won't simply one shot people like some of the other classes and your time to kill will be higher in general.
But what you lack in upfront damage, you make up with a plethora of movement and survival spells that, if played right, allows you to pretty much fight against any class in the game.
Don't get greedy, don't forget you are not really tanky despite wearing plate, and always try to create space when your AB is on cd.
You've got a whopping 45 range... USE IT


**Basic strat**
Engage in range to build up Scattered Stars.
At around 6-7 Star stacks, get in closer (either voluntarily or forced) to use Sentinel Glaive + Fan of Knives (if you are lvl 57+) + AB.
Spam LL 3-4 times continuously as the stacks are being consumed (if you didn't know, yes LL can be used multiple times after the first trigger - as long as there is still a Star stack on the oppoent).
Your auto attacks while using LL may give you another one or two Star stacks, which allows you get more LL off.
Use movement abilities to create space again and rinse and repeat.
Wardens are very squishy despite wearing plates, so don't fight toe-to-toe against real melee units for long.


**Combat tips**
- When in range of 20 yrds, spam Sentinel Glaive; should be used as soon as its off cd.
- Don't forget to use Lunar Eclipse/Moonwell Splash as soon as you lose a chunk of health.
You need the Lunar Eclipse stacks to keep building back up as you will need them to fight.
Treat it like another dps rotation; very high priority if you've lost enough health to use it.
- Avatar of Vengeance will make the rotation is easier, but against real melee units you will still be very squishy, so get out if your Astral Blade is on cd.
- Use Celestial Aegis while fighting in melee, especially if you have a high stack of Stars since they will give you more than enough mana back.
- Aspect of the Cosmos is used in most situations in order to stack Stars the fastest, but with the 5 sec cd, you can switch aspects as needed.
- Don't forget about the Command spell; great against hard casters like Stormbringer by forcing them to move.
- If you are OOM alot, you are probably not using your LL enough.
Always use it if you feel like your target is about to go out of range; you need that mana always topped up.
- If you are using NE (are you not role-playing as PotM???), don't forget about using Shadowmeld strategically both in and out of combat.
I love to use it on top of the mining entrance in Arathi; you have enough range to hit anyone targeting the banner if you stand right at the tip.
In combat it can be used to throw people off their rotation, especially if you are not dotted.


**Other tips**
- Always run the pvp trinket to break cc in addition to the Moonwell Water spell.
- Even though Intelligence is important for damage, never sacrifice your health for it.
Stamina is still king of pvp, so try to build a balanced build between Stamina and Intelligence (and Str if incidental) as that is often the most efficient stat build when it comes to equipment.
- Engineering will take your pvp to the next level but thats sweat tier.

[overview]
Basic talent build for engravement PvE. Make sure to read the talent section for the Single Target version; you only need to switch a few talents. 

I am by no means an expert, just passing on what I do know because our class does not have any builds posted. I will update this build as needed. 

Weapon Engravings:
AoE - Earth + Fire
Single Target - Frost + Fire (or Fire + Fire; with the macro in the macro section, you can apply two without swapping weapons, similar DPS though)

[talents]
Class talents are fairly loose; feel free to swap around some talents if there is something you think you'll need for the content you're doing. 

**Switching to Single Target: **
Remove Sky and Stone, Fists of Power, and Stone Savant and pick up Echoes of Eternity and Runelord; the last talent point is up to you; Symbols of Power 1/2 is a small DPS increase, Guarding Rune is probably better typically, unless you know you won't need the extra defensive; it is a very strong one.

If you feel like you need Guarding Rune in AoE for your group, I'd drop Mark of Strength or Explosive Runes. I've seen people drop Magic Etchings, but unless your group has a good armor reduction, I don't think it's a great idea; it helps a lot with boss damage from the group, and bosses can take a little while to kill.

[rotation]
Rotation is pretty simple, will probably get a little more complicated as we get more gear and can afford mana tax with Tattoo swapping. The goal is to get as many procs with your weapon engravings as possible. 

We are very strong as funneling our damage into a main target and passively AoEing the pack off that target, make sure you have a high priority target selected when cleaving. We also have one of, if not the very best kick in the game, it has a short cast time, but don't be weird, kick. 

**Tattoos**
You'll basically sit in Water forever; if you have a little more gear and can keep up on mana regen, feel free to swap into Fire and back to Water as needed. Don't forget swapping to Air removes a slow.

**AoE: **
Pop Zenith as much as possible; when Zenith is up remove Fist of Ancients from the rotation. 
Runic Brand for Marks and pop them with Runeblade; press Primordial Blast to reset Runeblade charges and hope for Runic Brand reset procs so you can keep popping marks. Weave in Fist of the Ancients when you have no Runic Brand stacks and Primordial Blast is on CD; the damage is kind of low, but the 20% engraving change is good. 

The idea is to try and keep up as many Runic Brand marks as you can and pop them for explosions and Wild Steams, and then rely on earth/fire procs from weapons to fill in the rest.  

**Single Target**
The rotation is not massively different from AoE, but the priority list shuffles a bit. Pop Zenith as much as possible; if you're the single target build, you'll have 2 charges. 
Primordial Blast moves up in priority to the top; it hits pretty hard in single target and helps stack armor pen ASAP. From there, try to keep Runic Blade marks up as much as possible; you'll pop them with your Runeblade as filler and press Primordial Blast on cooldown. Weave in Fist of the Ancients when Runic Blade and Primordial Blast are on CD.

- Greater [Sanguinary Offering](coa-skill:bloodmage:706630)- Greater [Bloodthorns](coa-skill:bloodmage:802313)- [Blood Shield](coa-skill:bloodmage:504296)

Rotation
- [Sanguine Rupture](coa-skill:bloodmage:800774) To Generate Rage On Multiple Targets.
- [Crimson Tide](coa-skill:bloodmage:504282) is a good skill to use if you have Excess rage in a Aoe Pull Because it will apply bleeds on up to 10 enemies which can Proc  [Spice Of Life] This combined with [Raging Hunger] Allows for massive rage generation and Pooled vitality  in aoe scenarios it also adds [Waves of Blood] Which can also proc  [Excess Blood].
- [Ravenous Strike](coa-skill:bloodmage:500123) Quickest single target rage generator, Also Allows you to proc [Adrenaline Boost] to get a instant [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) Both [Ravenous Strike](coa-skill:bloodmage:500123) (single target) and [Claw Sweep](coa-skill:bloodmage:500169) (Aoe) Can trigger this. and since both of these are cursed form abilities you proc [Dark Essence] at a 100% up time
- [Claw Sweep](coa-skill:bloodmage:500169) This Ability Costs 22 rage it's a good ability to use in aoe pulls to trigger [Dark Essence] and [Adrenaline Boost], while in aoe pulls you can use this in conjunction with [Sanguine Rupture](coa-skill:bloodmage:800774) to fish for both [Adrenaline boost] and [Crimson Scion](coa-skill:bloodmage:806424)
-  [Adrenaline Boost] This is a Talent, When using any of your melee cursed form abilities, if you crit it allows you to cast [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) or [Bloodmoon Blast](coa-skill:bloodmage:501607) as an instant cast.
- [Dark Essence] This is a Talent, When you use any of your cursed form abilities it will trigger an aoe Hot on your party as long as [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) is active, if you actively melee weave you will have a 100% uptime on Hot's also triggering [Adrenaline Boost]  for the instant cast [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781)
-  Casting [Dark Liturgy](coa-skill:bloodmage:800781) to apply [Blood Rituals](coa-skill:bloodmage:705729) is important so that you can use [Bloodmoon Blast](coa-skill:bloodmage:501607) for a party wide Heal while also generating rage (Single Target) While Stationary to avoid cleave mobs.
- Your Main Aoe heal is [Heartbreak](coa-skill:bloodmage:520314) This Costs 40 Rage.  If using this while Empowered it Gives 165 Attack Power/Spellpower To Party/Raid (Very good buff to keep up if you can fit it in.)
- Your main Single Target Heal is [Sanguine Mend](coa-skill:bloodmage:802310) This costs 20 Rage. If using this while Empowered it becomes a instant cast, and heals you for 50% of the heal value. Since we took [Predator] This ability now heals up to 2 people. and [Crimson Scion](coa-skill:bloodmage:806424) can proc when you do damage allowing you access to this ability as an instant cast.
- [Blood Veil] This is good to use Preemptively on a pull since it lasts 8 seconds or when your party is taking alot of damage, it shields them for 50% of incoming damage up to 1600 and gives you a bit of breathing room to generate rage or line up a [Heartbreak](coa-skill:bloodmage:520314) 
- [Fleshcraft](coa-skill:bloodmage:801952) This is your Panic button. It's Close to a lay on hands.
- [Shadow Vigil](coa-skill:bloodmage:806182) When someone in your party Rips threat or is taking alot of damage and they aren't a tank this will Give them an 8 second threat wipe.

- [Blood Tap] Is a ability that Sacrafices some health for 50% of your maximum rage.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Inspiration Guardian(PvE)
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
Welcome to Hell! I mean inspiration guardian, you've made the right choice coming here. Overly complex combos, random procs that determine if you sit there doing nothing or deal moderate dmg levels. It's a blast!

Strengths
- Raid wide buffs(5% crit/5% haste/5% rep/10% crit/10% dmg/10% healing/10%haste/+35% ap as adaptive/+145 adaptive/+15% dmg/10% physical crit dmg)
- Good damage output 
- High survivability and mobility 
- AOE CC & CC Immunity 
Weakness
- Damage is very RNG
- Peak damage isn't very high
- Complexity and stance swapping can be a major turn off

Note: Since writing this guardian has been updated a bit and there are currently four viable builds. This build has the best personal DPS of the builds in a majority of WB/ZG/Dungeons encounters.

[talents]
Most talents are pretty self explanatory going to discuss controversial ones

Feel free to swap Liberation for talents that may be useful for your group I.E. little drummer for stratholme
Inspiration Dissonance vs Song of steel. 
Song of steel cost 30 energy every 15 seconds and heavily slows down your combo. This is more useful in larger raids I.E. 20-40 man raids(it affects everyone in raid) or in heavy physical DPS comps. If you're doing dungeons/10 man raids, dissonance will give you and your party a lot more value especially if your group has more casters.

Voice of an Angel and Champion Presence - these are both extremely long CDs for very little return. For such a long cds we'll likely only get to use it once a fight it's not worth it compared to other options.

Valiant Warrior vs Grand Entrance - Grand Entrance can be a bit awkward to use, and although we stack strength making the AP values very attractive we also actively stack crit and are able to Empowered ram almost on CD. Along with the fact we don't have very high weapon scaling. After two ram procs Valiant Warrior will out value Grand Entrance.

Bannerman vs Echoes of War - Bannerman is currently bugged doing 0% extra damage on the initial tick and 300% extra damage(150% more for each banner) on every subsequent tick. Personally I run echoes of war in a raid setting, it can often be 2-5% of your raid members total damage contributing almost 4000dps by itself. Bannerman will give you a higher personal DPS output, and better dungeon damage.

[rotation]
We want to start most encounters in Line Formation this will allow us to open with **Harrowing Melody** and **advance**. Once we begin our rotation we want to swap and sit in **Assault stance** for the bonus crit and dmg.

**Jagged Reinforcement** when above 30% base crit(45% with banner + assault), **Weighted Reinforcement** when below this threshold.

We have a very simple opener 
Opener in question:
Advance + Standard of Supremacy/Valiance -> Harrowing Melody(run away after casting) + End Advance->  Battle drums(Try to cast between melee and caster groups) ->  Assault formation + Charge -> Macro(hero's March +  Chivlary + Inspiring Presence) + Glorious Arena -> Priority Rotation 
This opener takes about 3 seconds.

The main idea behind our rotation is pop all our cds, spam Dragonslayer/Conqueror until we get empowered ram and look for reprisal procs. Having a fast weapon will help out a lot with getting enough reprisal procs to not be sitting at 0 energy doing nothing.

Single Target - Priority
0. Standard of Valiance
1. Buffs: Hero's March/Chivalry/Inspiring Presence/Song of steel/Battle Drums
2. Harrowing Melody
3. Dragonslayer(If 3 or more mobs)
4. Empowered Ram(Cast at 2 tempo stacks)
5. Reprisal(/Inspiring Presence(When below 50 energy)
6. Glorious Arena
7. Ballad of the Conqueror

Note on casting harrowing melody mid combat, to go from assault, cast harrowing melody, and back to assault cost 70 energy returning effectively 105 energy worth of ballad cast. Have at least 70 energy casting from assault. 

Try to cast linebreaker in line with harrowing melody, this reduces energy waste from stance swaping and greatly benefits boss damage.

Dungeon:
During Dungeons I suggest alternating between inspiring Presence and Hero's March on pulls. While stacking them all is good on big pulls, when during small pulls alternate. This will gives you the most uptime of buffs, while maximizing cds so every minute you can pop one of these. Chivalry can be thrown in when you have packs large packs or elites.

Battle Drums should be used on dungeon bosses, don't pop it on trash packs unless it includes a boss. When doing raids try to place drums pre-pull to reduce energy waste or use them how the opener demonstrates. Using them mid raid boss is currently not viable because map clutter makes it very hard to notice/click them so only use them in your opener or pre-pull.

Raid: 
You are responsible for taking banners, other supports should take the 1% hit and armor versions. **ALWAYS COMMUNICATE WITH OTHER SUPPORTS WHAT TALENTS THEY ARE BRINGING, DO NOT OVERLAP**

[stats]
Expertise(Up to cap) > Hit(Up to cap) > Strength > Critical Strike  > Haste > AP > Armor Pen > agility

Everything you have scales off AP so strength to scale, we have naturally high crit rate and crit damage so it's not vital but will greatly boost dps and make ram less RNG. Hit and expertise up to cap.

[gear]
For weapons, we want weapons with a lot of stats.  All of our scaling comes for AP, so weapon damage is negligible. Try to proc  valiant effort as much as possible.

Recommended weapons: Warblade of the Hakkari(asc), Ancient Hakkari Manslayer(asc), Skullcrusher

Follow stat priorities for gear

[enchants]
Follow stat priority. Brutal Crusader on weapon.

[macros]
stance 1 line, stance 2 tower, stance 3 assault 
Example Macro
#showtooltip Harrowing Melody
/cast [nostance:1] Line Formation
/cast Harrowing Melody
/startattack
------------
#showtooltip Shield of Denial
/cast [nostance:1/2] Tower Formation
/cast Shield of Denial
/startattack
------------------
#showtooltip
/cast Hero's March
/cast Chivalry
/cast Inspiring Presence
/startattack

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Corruption Cultist PvP bg Leveling - Top DMG Every Time
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
Corruption Cultist is a DoT and burst caster with insane BG pressure, strong ST burst, good AoE, with crazy survivability

The basic playstyle is simple: DoT everything with Darkwither, spam Obliteration Beam and Gaze of C’Thun on CD, then delete priority targets with Psychic Suppression.

Because you have DoTs ticking on half the enemy team at the same time, this build almost always tops the dmg meter. It is especially broken in low-lvl BGs since you get strong defensives, healing, and AoE CC very early.

The talents shown in the build are the important core talents. The leftover points do not matter that much for leveling PvP, so you can move them around depending on what you prefer.

[rotation]
Your normal teamfight rotation in bg is:

Apply Darkwither to every enemy you see
Spam Obliteration Beam on CD
Use Gaze of C’Thun on CD
Drop your tentacle near enemy players
Use Psychic Suppression on a dotted target for huge burst
Keep tab-targeting and refreshing DoTs
If there are 3 or more enemies close together, use Eldrich Devastation
Spam sanity tap to get mana if needed or to reduce insanity.
NOTE (Update 2026/07/16) - new spell Eldrich Shock, use this on cd to reduce sanity


Do not tunnel one player too hard unless they are about to die. Your biggest strength is spreading pressure across the entire enemy team. Get your DoTs rolling first, then use your burst.

For your main ST burst:
Darkwither → Tentacle → Obliteration Beam → Gaze of C’Thun → Psychic Suppression 

Psychic Suppression is OP when the target is already dotted and your tentacle is down. It can take around 80% of someone’s HP and sometimes just kill them. Do not waste it on a target with no setup unless your team is near.

In a 1v1, you want to kite while your DoTs and tentacle do the work.

Apply Darkwither
Slow them with Grasp of Zek’voz - super op slow
Drop your tentacle
Spam Obliteration Beam and Gaze of C’Thun on CD
Keep moving and kite them
Use Psychic Suppression once everything is set up
If you get low, fear them and heal with Eldritch Mending

Against melee, do not just stand still. Slow, fear, kite, shield, and heal while your DoTs keep ticking.

Wrath of the Black Empire can also be worth casting in a 1v1 when the enemy is feared, heavily slowed, or unable to interrupt you. The normal cast time is very long, so do not try to hardcast it while someone is hitting you.

DEFENSIVES:

Spam Void Shield on CD!
Do not wait until you are almost dead. Keeping it active constantly makes you much harder to kill and stops a lot of random chip dmg.

Corrupt Mind is an insanely strong AoE fear. It can fear up to three players for eight seconds, which is completely broken in BGs.
An eight-second AoE fear can win an entire fight by itself.

Abyssal Ward is one of your big emergency defensives.
It has a long CD, so use it when you are getting focused or expect a large burst combo. Do not waste it on random low dmg.

Embrace the Void is another strong panic button with a long CD.
The problem is that it sometimes bugs, and you can still die through it. Do not rely on it.

Hallucination is best used to break out of slows, confuse enemy players and to get enemy pets or minions off you.
It is especially good when classes with pets or summoned minions are sitting on you, since it makes them drop target.

Eldritch Mending gives you really strong sustain.
If you get low, fear the enemy and heal. With correct use of Void Shield, fear, emergency defensives, and Eldritch Mending, you are basically unkillable unless several enemies jump you at once.

[stats]
Spell Power > Intellect > Haste > Stamina

At lower levels mana is a big issues so you might want prioritize int over spellpower.

[leveling]
When leveling try to rush all your darkwither talents then psychic suppression and glimpse of madness.

At lvl 18,28,38 and so on go to the capital PvP vendors to get honor gear. 

To level fast in bg try to stay close to teamfights and dot everything. You can easily kill efc with suppression and slow.

[tips]
You generally want to hit 60 Insanity because this gives you the 10% dmg increase.
This is easy to maintain since Darkwither, Obliteration Beam, and Gaze of C’Thun generate a lot of Insanity.
The important part is not accidentally going all the way to 100 Insanity.

Obliteration Beam is aoe so try to hit as many people as you can with it.

Below around lvl 40, you will probably have mana issues. This is where Sanity Tap becomes really useful.
Sanity Tap fixes both your mana problems and your Insanity management, so use it often.

Wrath of the Black Empire also lowers Insanity, but the cast time is normally way too long to use in the middle of a fight.
At 100 Insanity. When you hit 100, Wrath of the Black Empire cd is reduces a lot because you gain a lot of haste when at 100 insanity, even though this haste increase is not explained in-game or online from what I can tell.
So if you accidentally hit 100 Insanity, start spamming Wrath of the Black Empire if you are safe, otherwise pop defensive cd and run away untill it resets. 

When you unlock presence of yog, use that instead of presence of c'thun, it does quite a lot of dmg and is a pain against casters, and it works super well when you dot the entire enemy team. (Use servant of C'thun talent if you use c'thun)

If you like this guide and want me to do a corruption cultist PvE dungeon guide give this a fat thumbs or arrow up and let me know.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Incineration - Explode ST build
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
The build is focused on high single target damage and relies heavily on consecutive burst windows by building up full ember stacks and using [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) to spend and extend as much as possible, by using [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792).

**Please note that the build will not be updated any time soon, unless there are major changes/updates/buffs to the spec. At this point - Incineration is not a good spec. It can perform well, but talent combination and gameplay is boring and not rewarding. The spec urgently needs fundamental changes. It's better to play Draconic at this point.**

[talents]
The key talent about the spec is [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823).
The goal is to have very high burst single target windows, by spamming as much [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792) as possible and extending the duration of [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823).
As all the global cooldowns and casting time will be primarily taken by spamming [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792), the additional damage amplification will come passively from the burning DoTs.

You can take Sulfuron Harbringer instead of Heat Wave, but the damage increase/decrease is debatable, as there are not enough statistics to verify which is better.

[rotation]
**General rule of thumb:**
## 1. DoTs always need to be on the target, as they generate Heat and deal damage, as well as proc Sulfur Flames from Sulfuron Harbringer.
 - [Ignite](coa-skill:pyromancer:502020)
 - [Blaze](coa-skill:pyromancer:534600)
 - [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231) (Infernus passive)
 - [Scorched](coa-skill:pyromancer:704801) (Passive from direct critical strikes from Ember spenders like [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792))

## 2. Embers always need to be 3+(full before activating [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823)
 
### - If [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) is on cooldown follow this logic:
  - Less than 3 embers - use [Flare Bolt](coa-skill:pyromancer:502011)
  - More than 3 embers - use [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792)
 
### - If [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) is active follow this logic:
  - Spam [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792) until you run out of embers
  - If no embers are available, use [Meteor](coa-skill:pyromancer:500135) & [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231) or [Flare Bolt](coa-skill:pyromancer:502011) until enough for [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792).


## 3. [Meteor](coa-skill:pyromancer:500135) should be always used on cooldown.


## 4. Eruption should always be used together with [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) and racials, trinkets, etc.



***Burst window opener with full cooldowns and buffs(full ember stacks before pull):***
1. Start with [Ignite](coa-skill:pyromancer:502020)on the Target
2. Apply [Blaze](coa-skill:pyromancer:534600)
3. Cast [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231)
4. Cast [Meteor](coa-skill:pyromancer:500135)
5. Pop all cooldowns, buffs. - Eruption, [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823), Racial spell, Trinket, Potions
6. Start spamming [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792)
7. If you run out of Embers - cast [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231) and then continue with [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792)
8. If [Fired Up!](coa-skill:pyromancer:704823) is still active and has some time left and [Lava Shard](coa-skill:pyromancer:503231) is on cooldown - Use [Flare Bolt](coa-skill:pyromancer:502011) until enough for [Explode](coa-skill:pyromancer:800792) **or** re-apply your dots: [Ignite](coa-skill:pyromancer:502020), [Blaze](coa-skill:pyromancer:534600).

High critical items needed, as you need to crit as much as possible during Fired Up!

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Live, Laugh, Love Lunar Eclipse -> Moonflow
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
This is to maximise healing through Aspect of the Goddess !

Looking through Logs of Moon Priests I'm noticing a trend of spamming Lunar Eclipse -> Moonflow as much as possible, with very little Huntress Shots, and Moon Arrows going out - and that's not particularly a style I'm interested in playing. 

The goal isn't to drop Lunar Eclipse -> Moonflow, but to not force it to be the main heal when the Aspect can also do just as much, if not more healing when played around properly ! 

At 62.59 ilvl with 510 Int, 399 Bonus Healing: Aspect of the Goddess heals for 106, and Moonflow heals for 880. 

106 Healing per Ally × 5 = 530 Healing per Scattered Star Consumed

Realistically you're going to maintain 3 to 4 Stars:
3 stars → 1,590 Total Healing
4 stars → 2,120 Total Healing
6 stars → 3,180 Total Healing

This is before Tear Drops, Rampaging Waters, and any other buffs.

[talents]
Starcaller tree - 

Cosmic Duality + Moonwell vs Pouch of Stardust + Second Moon: 
Second Moon is adding about ~100 DPS in Raids
You will be overhealing a lot so Cosmic Duality kind of doesn't matter - it also doesn't provide a lot of DPS as the alternative. 
Moonwell is often an ability that I forget to use, and you don't really gain much from it. 
This is up to your comfort, and style that you want to play. 

Moonlit Lancer vs Lunar Anomaly: 
On bosses where you have to spam Lunar Eclipse -> Moonflow take Moonlit Lancer. 
Alternatively you can just take Moonlit Lancer and use Lunar Eclipse -> Moonflow as your main consumer then play around the burn.

Moon Priest tree -

With Lunar Revelation + Rampaging Water + Cycle of the Moon - Moonflow will have +25% chance to crit for Lunar Cascade to apply Eclipsing Arrow to the raid, allowing you to heal through Huntress Shot more. 

For Dungeons - 

Moonlit Lancer -> Lunar Anomaly 
Cosmic Duality + Moonwell -> Pouch of Stardust + Second Moon 
Lunar Revelation -> Elune's Favour
Lunar Cascade -> Celestial Form

Change between Moonwalk, and Twinkle Toes if you really care - I just leave it on Moonwalk, it's really not fun having to undo everything below it.

[rotation]
You'll be looping between Lunar Eclipse -> Huntress Shot to keep up Moonlit Lancer, and Lunar Eclipse -> Moonflow to heal, and apply Eclipsing Arrows to everyone. 

With enough Crit Lunar Eclipse is going to popping off where you can spam it with Huntress Shot more often. 

Try to keep at least 3-4 stars up at a time before consuming.

[leveling]
[Here's one of my comments, with builds about levelling as Moon Priest !](https://www.reddit.com/r/ProjectAscension/comments/1v5edq3/healer_indecisiveness/ozipkql/)

[macros]
Celestial Form, or Stellar Convergence are off the GCD so it's pretty safe to combine them since you'll almost always be using them together - be careful, if you spam it too much there's a bug where you'll remove Celestial Form: 

#showtooltip
/cast Celestial Form
/cast Stellar Convergence

You'll almost rarely be casting Moonflow without Lunar Eclipse, this macro stops mistakes from happening to avoid it from going on cooldown:

#showtooltip Moonflow
/cast Lunar Eclipse
/cast Moonflow

Moonwell: 

#showtooltip
/cast [@cursor] Moonwell

In case you're ever in melee:

#showtooltip
/cast Celestial Strike
/startattack

[tips]
With Lunar Swiftness early it allows you to Moon Arrow -> Moon Arrow -> Hand of Elune to keep up Tanks that are taking a beating. 

Rotate Celestial Form + Stellar Convergence on one pull, and Starshatter on the next - using Lunar Eclipse -> Moonflow to consume stars. These will replenish your mana to full, provide a lot of dps, and burst heal your group back up. 

Celestial Form really allows you to just spam Huntress Shot and Lunar Eclipse -> Moonflow without worrying about mana, so don't do anything else besides those two while you're in it.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Boltslinger - Twilight Frenzy AoE
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
This build specialises in AoE dungeon settings and is primarily using Twilight Frenzy for AoE and Witchbane for Single Target. If you've played Diablo III and enjoyed Demon Hunter, this could feel very familiar.
Build is highly effective provided the tank is pulling large packs of at least 3-4 mobs. Any less, and you won't have infinite rage to use Twilight Frenzy. 

**Pros:**
+High AoE capability
+Easy rotation
+High mobility
+AoE Stun/Silence

**Cons:**
-Spinning constantly
-Requires tank behaviour
-Poor survivability

## Abilities
**Spells used to deal damage: AoE**
1. Twilight Frenzy
2. Tormentor (with talent to spread it)
3. Caltrops
4. Shadow Trap
5. Scourge Frenzy

**Spells used to deal damage: Single Target**
1. Witchbane
2. Heartseeking Bolt
3. Tormentor
4. Scourge Trap
5. Shadow Trap
6. Death Trap
7. Brand of the Damned
8. Darkslayer

**Utility Spells:**
1. Shadow Trap - AoE stun (use to stabilise damage on tank)
2. Inquisitor's Trap - AoE silence (use on casters out of the pack) 
3. Caltrops - AoE slow (use to stabilise damage on tank)
4. Burrow Bolt - Drag that loose caster into the blender pack

**How to get more rage:**
1. Dark Regeneration
2. Tonics + Regenerative Elixirs talent in class tree
3. Darkslayer

[talents]
There are no Capstone talents for this build. The 25th point will go into Contract Killing. The majority of your casts will be Twilight Frenzy, and none of the Capstones play well with it during AoE sequences. You could pick up Bounty Hunter or Heavy Crossbows in its place for single target, but you'll get more out of Contract Killing overall in a dungeon setting.

**Tormentor + Strafing Shot:**
You can spread the Tormentor DoT to nearby enemies when you critically strike. This includes Twilight Frenzy. During AoE set up/the pull you can Darkslayer/Rage CD > Tormentor and then start Twilight Frenzy to spread. This will become even better when you hit level 50 (Tormenting the Tormented) and as you get more crit.

**Crossbow Frenzy:**
You will want the movement speed to keep up with certain tanks in a dungeon. Being able to catch up and use frenzy while the tank grabs more mobs to throw into the blender has very high potential damage.

**Everything you Have:**
More damage on Twilight Frenzy.

**Arbalest Mastery:**
On single target Witchbane is your main damage dealer. This will put a stacking debuff up to 10 on the target. Probably works with other WHs as well because it's a debuff on a target (ie Sunder). Get 50 rage and spam it. You can use Dark Regeneration/Tonics (with Regenerative Elixirs talent) to keep firing infinitely.

**Rapid:**
You don't need Witchbane to do AoE when you have Twilight Frenzy. Instead, make it Rapid so you can boost your boss and single target damage.

**Bane of Witches:**
Both Witchbane and Twilight Frenzy are physical damage. Heartseeking Arrow is primarily used on CD during Single Target for the +10% physical damage dealt. You may also get some use out of it as an effective filler cast while the tank is rounding up mobs and it isn't safe to Twilight Frenzy yet.

[rotation]
## AoE Rotation
While the tank grabs the mobs use Darkslayer once for rage or Heartseeking Bolt if you have more than 50 rage. Use Tormentor and then get ready to blend. Use Scourge/Shadow Trap once everything is stacked tight. Use Scourge Trap/Holy Water Tonic for undead/demons.

- Darkslayer/Heartseeking Bolt > Tormentor > Dark Regeneration/Holy Water Tonic > Twilight Frenzy until everything stacked > Scourge/Shadow Trap > Twilight Frenzy (until only 1 mob left)


## Single Target Rotation
You are keeping the Heartseeking Bolt +10% phys damage buff up on yourself, ensuring Tormentor is always ticking and using Witchbane as much as possible. Use your rage generators (tonics/Dark Regen) to avoid having to Darkslayer as required.

- Heartseeking Bolt > Tormentor > Dark Regeneration/Holy Water Tonic > Witchbane x6 > Refresh Tormentor + Caltrops > Refresh Heartseeking Bolt > Witchbane x6 > Refresh Tormentor

[macros]
**Twilight Frenzy:**
#showtooltip
/stopmacro [channeling:Twilight Frenzy]
/cast Twilight Frenzy
/stopcasting

**Caltrops:**
#showtooltip
/cast [mod:alt]Bola Throw;[@cursor]Caltrops

[tips]
Feeling overwhelmed by the amount of abilities? You can basically take Shadowblast off your bars.

You can cancel your Twilight Frenzy channel by using an instant cast.

Use your traps! The Scourge Trap is actually insane damage on Undead mobs and Brand of the Damned is basically a better Shadow Word: Death.

Some tanks get shitty when you start attacking before they've hit the mob. Just be aware and try to space yourself. If it's unsafe, don't Twilight Frenzy yet. Build some rage, get a Heartseeking buff. Ideally, the tank should be hitting the mobs as they run by so you can Twilight Frenzy almost immediately even as they continue to gather mobs up.

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: HH Spearheads on Foreheads
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
This build is great at single target, not very good at AoE but it does have a decent amount of cleave. You can move for the entire damage rotation though, so you can keep yourself safe in boss encounters or while kiting elites across the countryside in the open world.

[talents]
HH tree: Hunting for Sport, you should have near 100% uptime when you can set up and maintain your rotation. 20% armor pen is fantastic.
Barb tree: Savage Cadence and HH tree: Deep Fury are going to keep your Unbridled Rage up and available most of the time.

Barb tree: Outrage and Bloodthirsty, this is your big cooldown for a huge spike in damage. Once you get rolling and have enough crit you can keep it up for the duration of a fight.

HH tree: Gutspiller>Guts Splatter>To the Bone, this section of talents provide some great synergy that help you and your party both. Splatter gives you another source of 20% armor pen. To the Bone stacks a 20% armor sunder on the target that benefits the entire party.
HH tree: Legacy of Amani, great bonus damage when you get lucky. 
HH tree: Manhunter, you do 10% more damage vs humanoids, and everyone in your group gets 3% more crit. Quality point spent.

HH tree: Berserker and Sen'Jin's Guidance, Sen'jin's is where your rotation will finally make more sense. It will reset your Berserker Axe just like your other spears, but is not on the same cool down as your Spear abilities. Berserker is another boost (similar to Legacy of the Amani) that you won't have to worry about maintaining, it will just come naturally with your rotation.

[rotation]
Open with Unbridled Rage and Gutspiller. Gut spiller should be maintained, but not clipped because the final tick will be a Guts Spilled tick for more damage and a 4% sunder. 

Swing between burning Berserker Axe stacks or using a spear until you have to reapply Gutspiller
Use your 3 stacks of Berserker Axe. Berserker axe is going to reset after every spear while you are Enraged (should be 100%)
Javelin Toss (Sen'jin's guidance turns your throw weapon into a spear) does the most damage of the spears and is off the spear cooldown.
Headhunter's spear, decent damage, has no energy cost and bumps your energy up by 30%. Use this to keep from being energy starved. 

**the TL;DR**: Pop Outrage and macro in your Troll racial and trinkets.

**Single Target** - keep Unbridled Rage and Gutspiller rolling. Rotation starts 3 Berserker Axe > Javelin > 3 Berserker Axe > Headhunter's  spear and repeat the rotation.

For AoE - Carnage into Unbridled Rage then Spinning Axes into Gutspiller. 3 Berserker Axe > Impaling Spear > Onslaught if Carnage is down and you need to maintain energy > back to 3 berserker axe > Javelin and then repeat as best you can. You will run out of energy eventually and the real AoE classes will make you look silly anyways.

Maiming Spear is a utility for kiting and slowing down targets. 
Barbed spear is only better than Javelin if the target is being healed.

Impaling spear, decent AoE but has a wonky aiming mechanic similar to Cone of Cold or something. Make sure you are facing your target when you chuck it.

Sidenote, you can use your regular old Throw ability that everyone gets for a quick, no energy pop of damage. It works when you are standing still while spamming Berserker Axe. It is not on the same GCD as your abilities so you can just weave it in. Not much but I think its cool B)

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: Blessings Sun Cleric - Dungeons
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
Stance Dancing allows you to keep up with most DPS - especially after you add in Blessing of Absolution to your own dps !

This is a faster paced playstyle if you want to do as much dps as possible while providing your groups with a ton of healing.

[talents]
Change out Sanctified, and Faith for Everglow, and Sunbeams for Raids.

I don't think Cultivate Divinity + Empowered Holy Form is worth it because you'll probably not be casting Illumination a lot.

With more Haste - Gateway to Heaven becomes more attractive than Blazing Chariot - then your whole goal is to get in and out of Dawn as fast as possible. Though if you prefer a slightly slower playstyle then Blazing Chariot is still great !

You can take Unbreakable Focus, Suncharged (it does ~5% of your damage in dungeons), or Gleaming Vigil. 
I'm going with Unbreakable Focus combined with Final Vows, and Heaven's Appraisal it will allow you to get back into Vow of Dawn spam quicker. 

Enveloped in Light is a PvP talent since you're not going to be wearing much Mail and Plate at 60.

[rotation]
You'll want to be stance dancing as much as possible ! 

Solar Invocation: Conquest should be used on cooldown, and I think it's optimal to Radiant Conversion every time you're below ~85% mana. 

The rotation should be something like: 

Vow of Grace to build Solar Power -> Vow of Dawn + Dawn -> Sunflare / Heals -> Radiant Conversion + Conquest -> Vow of Grace -> Repeat

Your goal isn't to use all your stacks, but to maintain your mana as much as possible to keep spamming Sunflares inside of Vow of Dawn. Stance dancing, and using Radiant Conversion early with Conquest will allow you to get back into Dawn quickly. 

You rarely ever want to be building your own Solar Power, and that's why you always want to rely on Vow of Grace.

Vow of Grace and Vow of Dawn are the bread and butter, while Vow of Radiance should be used for the Dawn effect situationally - boss damage when you're not regenning, or to pump out massive heals when pulls go wrong.

Once you've picked up Dawnfall you can swap to Vow of Grace to get full mana every time you use Dawnfall. You can even wait for the last ~5 seconds, or as mobs are beginning to die to swap to Grace. 

Stand in melee to get as much Gavel of Grace, Judgement Day, and Radiance off as possible.

-

Once you get higher haste or two points into Guiding Glow - 

You can begin to cycle through Dawns very quickly for Gateway to Heaven: 

Start in Vow of Grace → Vow of Dawn + Dawn → 3-6 casts → Conquest + Radiant Conversion → 1-2 casts → Dawn again → 3-6 casts -> Radiant Conversion + Vow of Grace for 3-5 seconds -> Vow of Dawn + Dawn -> Repeat

When you have Conquest off cooldown stay in Vow of Dawn and Radiant Conversion at 10 or 9 stacks, or when Radiance ends - whichever happens first. 

It should be optimal to drop Dawn at any time around 10-8 stacks.

[gear]
This is the gear I'll be going for once I hit 60: https://coa.bisbeard.com/b/9Zegnfw8udGPVt

Haste should be incredibly bonkers to get in and out of Dawn or use its stacks, and to cast Sunflares faster

top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.title: The Frozen soul by " Exagelado" The troll Litch
top_build_detail_per_documented_spec.description:
[overview]
In this guide, you will learn where this subclass's damage comes from, as well as its different gameplay styles and the small choices that make a huge difference in your builds. I want to point out upfront that this guide is written entirely from my own perspective on the subclass and my personal gameplay experience—so feel free to share your thoughts, critiques, and suggestions!

[talents]
**Disclaimer**: 
## At level 30, the** "Frozen Power"** talent was replaced by the tree talent [Frigidness](coa-skill:necromancer:704669) which is no longer a 2-point talent, altering some aspects of the build path. Additionally, at level 50, the **"Champion of Kel'Thuzad"** talent was swapped for the tree talent[Permafrost](coa-skill:necromancer:704681) These updates, along with the change to the [Ice Barrage](coa-skill:necromancer:801760) skill proc, have significantly altered the gameplay style of this subclass, but I will do my best to share my opinion and experience.

**Class Tree:**
As a Necro - Rime, your goal in a fight is clear: you are an artillery tower. You don't have good mobility and have nothing beyond the freezing from your [Raise: Skeletal Mage](coa-skill:necromancer:500331) and [Ice Barrage](coa-skill:necromancer:801760) to keep enemies from reaching you. Embody this role completely. Against open-world PvE mobs, control the fights by freezing them to avoid taking damage, and use Fetid Ward to maintain good health sustain for both yourself and your undead minions.

So your class talent tree reflects this gameplay style. Although [Bone Tithe](coa-skill:necromancer:802121) is a good skill in other subclasses, it’s fairly useless in this one—I consider it a wasted talent point. Let me explain: in PvE, you don't want the mob getting close to you, and your arsenal provides you with the tools to prevent that. Don't forget that your playstyle is very similar to a Demonology Warlock combined with a Frost Mage, but without Blink—**you are an artillery tower.**

Talents focused on boosting the power of your **Lich Bolt** and your **undead minions**, as well as providing extra sustain during fights like using your reliquaries, are the way to go. Your Abomination will be your best friend because it’s your personal tank; it absorbs the damage while you lock enemies down from afar and deal damage. Your class tree essentially acts as a support tree for your subclass, and I won't lie: until level 40, you are very weak. Your gameplay is basically that of a Frost Mage with a personal tank.

Additionally, in dungeons, you don't need sustain—what you need is massive AoE damage and, above all, **single-target damage**, which is where this subclass truly shines and dominates.

**Subclass Tree:** 
The previously mentioned changes to both your [Ice Barrage](coa-skill:necromancer:801760) skill and your talents give you three available gameplay styles:

1- [Raise: Skeletal Mage](coa-skill:necromancer:500331), focused on your undead minions' critical damage alongside your own massive damage.

2- **AoE and Stacking Damage**, using your [Glacial Impact](coa-skill:necromancer:704355) and the **Frozen Bodies** talent paired with the undead horde from the Army of the North talent. It's important to mention that area damage isn't the strong suit of this subclass—Animator and especially Death do this much better—yet its AoE damage is still good, consistent, and useful.

3- **Massive Single-Target Critical Damage**. There isn't much to say about this last one—it's very straightforward.

You can choose one of these options (1, 2, or 3) as your main path and take half of another to "support" your primary damage source. **(I say "support" because playstyle 3 can significantly boost the damage of the other two, making it virtually essential. However, it's fair to say that if you just want nonstop area damage, you can mix 1 and 2 and rely on crit RNG.)**

Once you've chosen your style—and to make this guide easier to follow—I'll share my own setup, which combines 1 and 3. This means continuous critical damage from my skeletal mages **(who deal AoE damage in dungeons when enemies are stacked together)** by using talents to boost their crit chance and frost projectile damage, paired with style 3 to deal absurd amounts of single-target damage yourself. It's worth noting that I chose to empower [Lichfrost](coa-skill:necromancer:801722), [Ice Barrage](coa-skill:necromancer:801760), and [Glacial Impact](coa-skill:necromancer:704355), turning them into more consistent damage sources throughout gameplay. Talents focused on increasing your maximum Runic Power are also extremely useful.

Choice Talents and Why:

**[Necrotic Chains](coa-skill:necromancer:801733) or [Ner'zhul's Blessing](coa-skill:necromancer:704729)
A very simple question to answer. Do you prefer a guaranteed critical hit on a damage spell, or a snare that breaks on the very first hit of damage taken? The choice is clear.

**Frigid Death or Freeze Dry?**
Honestly, an extra 50% damage combined with the talent directly below it, Glacier Lord—which guarantees a 100% critical strike on Glacial Impact when the enemy is frozen—made me prefer the raw damage. But if you think getting 20 additional Runic Power after casting is worth it, feel free to take Freeze Dry.

**Lastly, Blood and Ice or Death and Ice?**
Death and Ice grants a flat 10% critical chance to your [Raise: Skeletal Mage](coa-skill:necromancer:500331)—and I say "yours" in the plural because your goal is to reach the Grave Mages talent. This talent reduces the cost of mages from 2 Life Force down to 1, allowing you to field 3 of them at once, each with a guaranteed 10% critical chance for every Frostbolt they land on the target(s). The other option increases the damage of your [Ice Barrage](coa-skill:necromancer:801760)—which deals high, consistent damage—but to trigger the talent, you need to have [Command: Skeletal Warriors](coa-skill:necromancer:504334)or Rogues active. You could run 1 Mage and 1 Rogue, for example, since it only triggers one at a time. But again: you're looking at 3 units of one of the strongest undeads in the Necromancer's entire arsenal, so think carefully.

[rotation]
Cast Lichfrost until your Runic Power bar is full. Whenever your Permafrost procs during the cast, make sure to use it! Once your Runic Power bar is full, use your mage's Undead Command, and when the instant cast for Ice Barrage procs, use it—freeze the enemy and follow up with Glacial Impact. Keep doing this until your bar is drained, then repeat.

If you are fighting more than 3 enemies (in a dungeon or raid), choose 2 targets and apply Blight, then resume the rotation mentioned earlier while holding back on Ice Barrage. Most of your AoE damage will come from your mages' Undead Command and Blight.

If you are facing a very strong enemy (like a boss), I recommend using a macro to activate all your temporary undeads at once. I'll leave the macro right here:

/cast Unholy Frenzy

/cast Berserking(Racial) (I'm a Troll)

/cast Gravebound Champion

/cast Icebound Champion

/cast Spellbound Champion

Once you have this horde beating down on a single enemy, you can punish them with the initial rotation mentioned earlier. (Adding Animate: Frost Wyrm to this macro can be really good, but keep in mind that this dragon deals AoE damage, so saving it for the AoE rotation might be a better choice.)

[stats]
I'm still not entirely sure about stat priorities, but Critical Strike and Intellect don't have a soft or hard cap. As for Hit, you'll need 17% (though keep in mind we get a passive 4% from our class tree). Spell Power scales exceptionally well in this subclass, unlike Haste, which works much better in the other two subclasses but not as much here—we can deal massive damage since our SP scaling is significantly higher thanks to our talents. Plus, every time we land a critical strike, we restore a bit of mana, making our mana management very predictable.

So once you're Hit Capped, the stat priority is: SP > Crit > Intellect > Haste

[leveling]
It's a great build for leveling, but I have to warn you that until level 40—when you get Lich Form—the gameplay feels quite slow, static, and repetitive.

[macros]
Use this macro to command your undeads to attack the target while you cast Lichfrost:

/cast Grave March
/cast Lichfrost

I recommend using a macro to activate all your temporary undeads at once. I'll leave the macro right here:

/cast Unholy Frenzy

/cast Berserking(Racial) (I'm a Troll)

/cast Gravebound Champion

/cast Icebound Champion

/cast Spellbound Champion
